enrichments.description:
Allen the Alien, or commonly known as Allen, is a major character in Invincible. He is the boyfriend of Telia.

Born in a Unopan breeding facility created to replenish his race after the Viltrum Empire nearly eradicated them, and also to act as a defense against the Viltrumites. Although his function as a defense against the Viltrumites was ineffective, he later assumed the position of a Coalition of Planets' evaluation officer, traveling to different planets in multiple galaxies in search of a warrior capable of defeating the Viltrumites. After a close brush with death, Allen gained increased strength and was able to compete with the strongest Viltrumites. After recruiting Invincible, he managed to bring his father, Nolan, on board so they could unitedly work together to bring the Empire's reign of terror to a permanent end. In the aftermath of the Viltrumite War, Allen was named the new leader of the Coalition after Thaedus' death. Learning that the remaining Viltrumites are on Earth, Allen attempts to unleash the improved Scourge Virus onto the planet to end their race, even at the cost of Earth's inhabitants.

Allen is a tall humanoid of fairly large muscular build and orange skin. He is characterized by diminutive pointed ears and a prominent large eye on his face, featuring a white sclera and a tiny, horizontal rectangle for a pupil. A thick, protruding brow shields over his eye. Allen's face has a square shape and a prominent chin. He possesses three digits on each hand: one thumb, one digit serving as a substitute for the index and middle fingers, and another digit acting as a replacement for the ring and little fingers. He also possesses just three thick toes.

After recovering from his near-death encounter against the Viltrumites, Allen's body became significantly enhanced, growing much taller and equal growth in muscle mass, the latter highlighted by noticeable definition.

enrichments.description:
Anissa is a major antagonist in Invincible, debuting from Season 2 and onwards.

She is the most powerful female Viltrumite warrior of the Viltrum Empire, committed to its mission of universal domination. Shortly after Viltrum's destruction, Anissa resettled into Earth's human society to find suitable mates to interbreed with and repopulate the Empire.

Anissa is a tall woman with tan skin, striking blue eyes, and short black hair that frames her high cheekbones. Widely regarded as exceptionally beautiful, she possesses an athletic yet curvaceous figure. Her physique is well-defined, showcasing prominent muscle tone, particularly in her shoulders and upper arms.

As one of the Empire's highest-ranking warriors, Anissa wears a high-ranking Viltrumite uniform featuring a refined variation of the traditional emblem, reflecting her elite status.

enrichments.description:
Thokk, better known as Battle Beast, is a supporting character in Invincible, debuting from Season 1 and onwards.

He is a legendary Dornian warrior driven by an insatiable desire to find worthy opponents who can grant him a glorious death in battle. His unyielding thirst for conflict led him to Earth, where he met, fought, and bested Invincible and the Guardians of the Globe. In the end, he deemed them inadequate and departed the planet. Not long after, he was imprisoned by the Viltrum Empire, but nearly a year later, he was freed by Allen the Alien to unite with the Coalition of Planets in their effort to finally defeat the Empire so he might battle the strongest Viltrumites.

Battle Beast is a tall, powerfully built humanoid alien with striking leonine features. His body is covered in white fur, and his mane is styled into French braids along both sides of his head. He wears a black leotard with red shoulder pads, black arm warmers, red toeless boots, and matching gloves. A distinctive belt with a red-and-yellow checkered pattern completes his appearance. He is likely a member of the same species as Mokk, as both share similar feline, lion-like characteristics.

Battle Beast is a fierce, relentless leonine warrior driven by an insatiable, exhilarating thirst for worthy combat. Proud and arrogant, he views most inferior opponents as beneath his level, often showing disdain and cruelty toward those he deems weak or unworthy of facing his raw might. His brutal and ferociously efficient fighting style displays superior strength and tactical prowess, intimidating even the most formidable foes. Battle Beast’s passion for battle borders on being obsessive, even nigh suicidal, as he yearns for a true warrior’s death at the hands of a worthy, superior adversary.

Cecil Stedman is one of the three overarching protagonists (alongside Thaedus and The Immortal) of Invincible, debuting from Season 1 and onwards.

For decades, he has served as the director of the Global Defense Agency, responsible for coordinating Earth's defense against superpowered threats and working alongside heroes such as the Guardians of the Globe and Omni-Man. Following the massacre of the Guardians, he led an investigation that determined Omni-Man was responsible. With the assistance of Invincible, Omni-Man was stopped before completing his objective of conquering Earth. After Omni-Man's departure following the destruction of Chicago, Cecil focused on strengthening Earth's defenses against future threats. His efforts included developing the ReAnimen and continuing Invincible's training to prepare for a potential Viltrumite invasion. Although his pragmatic methods caused great tension with Invincible, the two continued to cooperate during major crises, including the Invincible War.

Following the defeat of Conquest, Cecil secretly detained him in The Block for interrogation and experimentation in an effort to develop countermeasures against the Viltrum Empire. Two weeks later, a fully healed Conquest easily escaped, but Cecil kept his survival a secret from Invincible to avoid his wrath. Shortly after, the Flaxans returned to conquer Earth once more. This ended in failure but resulted in Robot and Monster Girl being trapped in the Flaxan Dimension. Cecil and the G.D.A. repeatedly attempted to rescue them but failed at every turn. Following the Viltrumite War, Nolan and Cecil tenuously reunited. Upon learning that the remaining Viltrumite still posed a danger to Earth, Cecil ordered Nolan to leave the planet, instructing him to return only if his people arrived. Additionally, Cecil began collaborating with Invincible on how to handle the looming threat of the Viltrum Empire.

enrichments.description:
3x07 "What Have I Done?" (Debut)}} Conquest was a major antagonist in Invincible, debuting from Season 3 to 4.

As one of the most powerful figures in the Viltrum Empire, Conquest was a high-ranking veteran warrior. Approximately dedicated to its mission of universal domination, he served as the Viltrumites’ fundamental "nuclear option," deployed only when maximum force and absolute ruthlessness were deemed necessary. As instructed, Conquest went on a mission to determine whether Invincible had fulfilled his duty on Earth. However, he was ultimately defeated by him and imprisoned by the Global Defense Agency. Upon recovery, Conquest fled back to his superiors to face the consequences of his failure. Thragg spared Conquest's life, giving him a final chance at redemption by hunting down the traitors: Nolan and his son, Invincible. At the peak of the Viltrumite War, he was finally felled by Invincible in their final battle, before being given a proper burial by Nolan.

Conquest was a towering, elderly Caucasian Viltrumite with a commanding presence, standing at approximately 6’8”. Like all adult male Viltrumites, he sported a thick, well-groomed mustache. His advanced age was evident even by Viltrumite standards, marked by deep wrinkles, balding gray hair, and crooked teeth. Despite his aged appearance, Conquest maintained an imposing, massively muscular physique.

During an incident on the Savage Planet, while his regenerative abilities were temporarily impaired, Conquest sustained severe injuries. A deep, disfiguring scar runs diagonally from his left temple, across his right eye, blinding it, and down his right cheek. His right arm was severed just below the bicep during a brutal encounter with a Rognarr and later replaced with a cybernetic prosthetic. The predominantly bronze mechanical arm features silver accents and glowing amethyst lights.

enrichments.description:
Robert Kirkman is the creator of the Amazon Prime Video series Invincible and the co-creator of the comic book series it is based on (alongside Cory Walker and Ryan Ottley).

He also co founded Skybound Entertainment.

His favorite episode of the series is “I'm Not Going Anywhere”. In the creator's own words: "Episode 7 of Season 2 has a scene that I've been dying to adapt from the comics into the show. I can't wait for people to see the way that we changed it because it couldn't be done in the same way. I'm speaking in code now because of the way it is in the comics. We had to change it completely, and so we kind of had to like rebirth a fan-favorite iconic scene in a way that works in animation. So it's the same, but it's 100% fundamentally different. So I wanna see if it has the same effect and is as beloved."

enrichments.description:
The Viltrum Empire are the main antagonistic faction of Invincible.

Founded and led by the first Emperor, Argall, the Empire is comprised of Viltrumite warriors dedicated to expand its dominion across the galaxy and ultimately the entire universe.

An elite protective unit tasked with safeguarding the Emperor or the Grand Regent. Members are selected from among highly skilled Viltrumite warriors and are distinguished by their red ceremonial uniforms, often featuring hooded designs and modified insignia. Their role is ceremonial and defensive rather than administrative or command-based, and they operate directly under the authority of the Emperor. Though, this later became defunct in the aftermath of the Scourge Virus.

While Viltrumite uniforms follow a standardised design, variations in insignia are used to visually distinguish individuals of exceptional status within the Empire. Elite warriors, military commanders, and high-ranking officials may wear uniforms featuring refined variations of the traditional Viltrumite emblem, representing their authority, achievements, and recognition among the Empire’s highest ranks. These variations are distinguished by additional design elements incorporated into the original emblem.
enrichments.short_description: The Viltrum Empire are the main antagonistic faction of Invincible.

enrichments.description:
Viltrumites are a highly advanced alien race of exceptionally powerful superhumanoids native to their destroyed home planet, Viltrum. As the dominant species of the Viltrum Empire, they pursue an expansionist doctrine aimed at universal conquest and absolute dominion over other civilizations. They are feared across the known universe as a disciplined but merciless militaristic society that is driven by ideological supremacy and the belief that strength determines legitimacy.

Under the first Emperor, Argall, Viltrumite ideology was formalized into a disciplined imperial doctrine emphasizing strategic thinking alongside martial supremacy. This created a thoroughly coordinated expansionist civilization in which conquest, governance, and cultural enforcement operated as unified systems. Argall's legacy officially established the principle that only the strong may shape the future of the Empire, a doctrine that would later be intensified under Grand Regent Thragg.

thumb|left|200x200px|Through Argall's tactical wisdom, his people were guided to reach the heights of their potential. thumb|left|200x200px|Thragg|Thragg proved himself to be the epitome of Viltrumite traditions. thumb|left|200x200px|Even long after his death, the Viltrumites continue to follow Argall|Emperor Argall's wisdom. thumb|left|200x200px|Viltrumites such as Conquest can be reduced to hopelessly unstable, bloodthirsty beasts. A key feature of Viltrumite culture is an extreme form of Darwinism supported by rigid discipline and a belief in their own racial superiority. Established under Emperor Argall, their society judged individuals by strength, capability, and usefulness. Weakness was considered both a liability and a threat to the Empire, with those deemed unfit often eliminated to preserve the species' overall strength. Viltrumites emphasize measured power, tactical effectiveness, and the disciplined appeal of force rather than indiscriminate brutality, ensuring stability and imperial cohesion while reinforcing the belief that the weak are expendable.

The expansion of the Viltrum Empire is driven not only by conquest but also by the belief that Viltrumites possess a natural right to rule over lesser species. Their social hierarchy is based primarily on demonstrated strength and ability. Conquered worlds that prove useful may be integrated into the Empire and granted technological or infrastructural advancement in exchange for complete obedience. Those that continue to resist are often subjected to military suppression, large-scale devastation, or outright extermination.

enrichments.description:
The Global Defense Agency (G.D.A.) is a covert paramilitary organization, law enforcement body, and intelligence agency tasked with monitoring and neutralizing global superhuman threats. Operating from a subterranean headquarters beneath the Pentagon in Arlington, Virginia, the G.D.A. maintains strong ties to the United States federal government, though its operational jurisdiction extends worldwide.

The agency is responsible for shielding Earth from criminal, extraterrestrial, paranormal, and supernatural crises. To combat organized super-crime, supervillain terrorism, kaiju attacks, and alien invasions, the G.D.A. directly bankrolls the Guardians of the Globe and frequently contracts independent superheroes across the planet.

The Global Defense Agency is primarily funded and staffed by the United States, yet its operational reach transcends all national borders. Armed with global assets, the G.D.A. can project power from the deepest expanses of outer space to the underwater kingdom of Atlantis.

To neutralize threats, monitor superpowered entities, and safeguard Earth, the G.D.A. deploys a vast arsenal of cutting-edge facilities, specialized vehicles, and advanced technology, much of which is of highly questionable ethical origin. These technological assets are engineered to supplement, or entirely substitute for, the capabilities of traditional superheroes.

The Guardians of the Globe are a superhero team of extraordinary individuals, considered to be the best of the best. Their purpose is to protect the Earth from both internal and extraterrestrial threats. Though primarily affiliated with the Global Defense Agency, they operate on a global scale rather than in a specific region.

The Immortal is a Celtic warrior that was granted immortality, along with flight, super strength, and durability, from a mysterious spiral of energy. After several millennia living various lives among the human race, he became a superhero and leader of the original Guardians of the Globe. Along with his fellow teammates, he was eventually betrayed and killed by Omni-Man, being punched through the stomach before being decapitated. The Mauler Twins later revived him, at which point, Immortal sought out and battled Omni-Man in a rematch, one which ended with Immortal once again being killed, this time via bisection. His body was later recovered by the Global Defense Agency, who sought to revive him once more. A month after Omni-Man left Earth, the G.D.A. had successfully resurrected him and he was once again put in charge of the Guardians of the Globe, replacing Robot. Not long after his engagement to Dupli-Kate, the two of them decided to retire though both are briefly called back to action during the Invincible War.

enrichments.description:
The Coalition of Planets (C.O.P.) is an intergalactic peacekeeping organization dedicated to stopping the Viltrum Empire from taking over the universe. Led since its foundation by its founder, Great Thaedus. Upon his death, Thaedus' most trusted subordinate Allen of Unopa was made his successor of the Coalition, as per his wishes.

After the conclusion of the Viltrumite War, the Coalition achieved its objective of freeing the universe from the Empire’s control and shifted its focus to protecting all known worlds from potential new dangers.

enrichments.description:
Earth is the main setting of Invincible and the home planet of the human race, which coexists alongside other intelligent species.

Earth is the densest planet in the solar system, the largest terrestrial body in its system, and a marine world where water traditionally covered roughly 71% of its mountain-and-valley landscape.

Earth’s sociocultural system is a hyper-volatile, multi-layered civilization where a mundane, capitalist human society coexists with existential sci-fi and supernatural anomalies, all stabilizing under the utilitarian hegemony of the Global Defense Agency. Led by Cecil Stedman, this shadow state operates with extreme moral ambiguity, manipulating international politics and weaponizing reformed villains to maintain a fragile status quo. Within the public sphere, superheroes are highly institutionalized as both critical national security infrastructure and heavily commercialized, media-managed celebrities, fostering a civilian population defined by a state of profound cognitive dissonance. Regular people aggressively pursue normal lives, going to school, working retail, and paying bills, while treating city-leveling battles like severe weather events, where survival simply means returning to a normal work week the very next day. For the superhero community, this creates an exhausted, 24/7 bureaucratic grind of hyper-vigilance and psychological trauma.

This surface-dwelling society shares the planet with sovereign, isolationist species, such as the monarchical Atlanteans and subterranean Magmanites, all while looming under the existential threat of the Viltrum Empire. This Darwinistic warrior race infiltrates Earth's culture to assess its defenses, ultimately viewing human existence with contempt, yet its unique emotional depth acts as a psychological trap powerful enough to subvert centuries of rigid imperial conditioning in Viltrumites who stay too long.
enrichments.short_description: Earth is the main setting of Invincible and the home planet of the human race, which coexists alongside other intelligent species.

enrichments.description:
Viltrum was the home planet of the Viltrumites and the capital of the Viltrum Empire. At the peak of the Viltrumite War, the Coalition of Planets united to destroy the world, leaving the remaining Viltrumites homeless and their empire without a capital.

Viltrum was a terrestrial planet similar to Earth in composition, but far larger. Prior to the Scourge Virus, Viltrum was an awe-inspiring, sun-lit paradise of fascist perfection, boasting bright blue skies, crystal-clear air, and a pristine landscape dominated by towering, sterile white marble skyscrapers and grand geometric monuments that reflected the empire's absolute supremacy. Following the deployment of the devastating bioweapon, the planet underwent a apocalyptic transformation. After the virus eradicated 99.9% of the population, leaving around fifty pure-blooded survivors, the complete lack of maintenance and industrial collapse caused the automated climate systems to fail, mutating the atmosphere into a hellscape of blackened skies, raging electrical storms, and toxic green smog. The planet became an empty, automated graveyard, most disturbingly marked by a massive, literal planetary ring composed entirely of the frozen, floating corpses of the billions of Viltrumites who had coughed up blood and perished from the disease, forming a permanent, macabre halo around their dying homeworld.

Viltrumite society was a terrifyingly efficient social Darwinist monarchy built on a foundation of fascist eugenics, absolute totalitarianism, and galactic imperialism; however, its structural core shifted dramatically from the historical Argall Era to the ruthless regime of Grand Regent Thragg. Under the benevolent yet imperialistic rule of Emperor Argall, Viltrum experienced its legendary "Golden Age," a period focused on unifying fragmented factions, advancing planet-wide technology, and establishing a supreme royal bloodline based on hereditary authority and perceived wisdom. Conversely, Thragg’s era abandoned institutional stability for raw, brutal militarism; following Argall's assassination by the betrayer Thaedus, Thragg capitalized on the tragedy to initiate "The Great Purge," a horrific civil war that systematically slaughtered nearly half of the planet's own population to root out perceived physical and ideological weakness. While Argall sought a thriving, structured civilization that subjugated other worlds through dynastic right, Thragg's regime transitioned Viltrum into a fragile, desperate, and fiercely aggressive militant empire, one forced to conceal its severe population decline caused by the subsequent Scourge Virus, shifting the cultural definition of a leader from royal lineage to absolute, uncontested physical strength.

Viltrum was composed of Viltrumite males and females, led by the wise but cold-hearted Argall, who helped establish an era of paradise in their golden age, creating technology and medicine that he would expand to the galaxy. Viltrumites erected statues; one with a book, another placed in his very own fortress. It was said that only he was given and deserved statues because of his supposed perfect leadership.

enrichments.description:
The Sequids are recurring antagonist in the series making their debut in the first season.

They are a parasitic alien species known for their destructive nature and their iconic ability to control the minds of others, having left a trail of devastation across the universe before ultimately crash-landing on Mars. During their time on Mars, the Sequids were enslaved by the Martians since they required living and controllable hosts in order to become a true threat.

That situation changed when a group of astronauts arrived on Mars, with Invincible following the mission. The Sequids managed to take control of one astronaut, Rus Livingston, using him as a host to break free. They quickly unified, destroyed Mars, and then set their sights on Earth.

Their first attempt to invade Earth was stopped by the combined efforts of the Guardians of the Globe, along with Atom Eve and Invincible, who was able to save Rus. However, one Sequid secretly remained inside him and later took control again, quietly building up hosts for another invasion.

enrichments.description:
The Immortal is a supporting character in Invincible. He is an immortal superhero who has lived for thousands of years and left a significant mark on human history, assuming numerous identities throughout his life. Among these, he lived as a medieval knight, possibly associated with Arthurian legend, and later as Abraham Lincoln, before eventually adopting the superhero identity of the Immortal in the early 20th century, becoming the world's first official superhero.

He was a member of the original Guardians of the Globe and the only member to eventually return after the team was murdered by Omni-Man. Following his resurrection, the Immortal joined the newly formed Guardians and later assumed leadership of the team, replacing Robot. During this period, he also entered a relationship with Dupli-Kate, who, out of all his previous lovers, understood his struggle with experiencing death recurrently.

Following Kate's apparent death by the Komodo Dragon and his own struggles as a leader, the Immortal temporarily stepped away from the Guardians while grieving her loss. After discovering that Kate had survived, the two reunited and eventually became engaged. He subsequently returned to active duty and continued serving with the Guardians through the events of the Invincible War. In the aftermath, the Immortal retired alongside Kate, leaving superhero work behind so that the two could start a family together.

The Immortal is a tall, fair skinned man with jet-black hair, blue eyes, and a full beard with a clean-shaven upper lip. He has strong, angular facial features and a large, well-defined muscular build.

enrichments.description:
Thragg is the main antagonist of Invincible, debuting from Season 4 and onwards.

He is the most powerful Viltrumite and the current Grand Regent of the Viltrum Empire, having formerly served as Regent under Emperor Argall before assuming leadership following Argall’s death at the hands of the Betrayer, Thaedus. As his first order, Thragg initiated the Great Purge to erase weakness and disloyalty within Viltrumite society, before resuming the empire’s mission of universal domination, the hunt for Thaedus, and locating Argall’s missing heir. Nearly a millennium later, Thragg avenged Argall by killing Thaedus in the climax of the Viltrumite War. Following the destruction of Viltrum, the empire’s expansion was halted by an uneasy truce on Earth with Invincible, permitting the Viltrumites to survive and rebuild.

Thragg is a tall, fair-skinned man with a broad, muscular build and a powerful, well-defined physique. He has short black hair cut in a buzz cut style, brown eyes, and, like most adult male Viltrumites, wears a thick, well-groomed black mustache.

After being appointed Regent under Emperor Argall, Thragg wore a high-ranking Viltrumite uniform featuring a refined variation of the standard Viltrumite emblem, reflecting his high rank and trusted status within the Empire prior to becoming Grand Regent.

enrichments.description:
Rex Connors, formerly known as Rudolph "Rudy" Connors, is a major character in Invincible, debuting from Season 1 and onwards.

Born with severe physical deformities and critical health problems, Rudy Connors was an exceptionally intelligent human scientist trapped inside a compromised body. To bypass his physical limitations, he developed a highly advanced, combat-ready drone system, operating for years under the superhero moniker Robot. After successfully leading the Teen Team, Rudy was recruited into the new Guardians of the Globe following Omni-Man's brutal slaughter of the original roster. Everything changed when he fell in love with his teammate, Monster Girl. Desperate to live a normal life with her, Rudy manipulated the Mauler Twins into cloning a healthy human body using a blood sample from Rex Splode. He successfully transferred a copy of his consciousness into this clone to begin a new life, while his original, frail body peacefully passed away.

With the love and support of Amanda/Monster Girl, the cloned Rudy adapted to his new humanity while continuing to protect Earth. When the devastating Invincible War struck, Rex Splode tragically sacrificed his life to save him and their fellow teammates. Deeply moved by the loss, Rudy legally adopted Rex's first name as a permanent tribute to his fallen friend. Not long after the funeral, the alien Flaxans launched another invasion of Earth. Though Rudy and Monster Girl successfully drove the invaders back, their counter-strike pulled them through a dimensional rift, leaving the two heroes stranded inside the Flaxan Dimension for what would become an agonizingly long era.

Originally, Robot was a severely deformed human, barely larger than a child and crumpled inside a liquid-filled pod with mechanical legs. His skin was pale and covered in sores and blisters, his nose hidden (or replaced) by a mechanical clamp, and his only working eye was the yellow-green right eye.

Amanda, better known by her superhero alias Monster Girl, is a major character in Invincible, debuting from Season 1 and onwards.

Originally operating under the moniker Monster Woman, Amanda emerged as a core member of the new Guardians of the Globe following Omni-Man's brutal massacre of the original team. She possesses the incredible ability to transform into a towering, formidable beast, granting her immense superhuman strength and durability. However, this power carries a devastating curse: every transformation permanently regresses her biological age, leaving her trapped in the body of a young girl despite being 26 years old. Her tragic isolation finally ended when Robot engineered advanced scientific technology to halt her regression, allowing a deep romance to blossom between them.

enrichments.description:
Several variants of the Mauler Twins appear as overarching antagonists in Invincible Season 2. While they share many traits with the original Mauler Twins, they come from alternate universes and exhibit distinct differences.

Most of them were voiced by Kevin Michael Richardson, but the voice actress of the Female Mauler is currently unknown.

The Mauler Twins or at least countless variants of themselves were summoned by Angstrom Levy to stop Invincible from interfering with his plans. After four of them had him pinned and weakened, they took it to far and nearly killed Invincible, resulting in their own demise. Angstrom removed his helmet that severed the connection to the machine meant to transfer knowledge from his variants, despite the pleas from the fools, thus the building imploded with all of them in it. Their burned corpses were seen afterwards, confirming their demises.

While all of the Mauler variants were killed, the mainstream Mauler Twin survived after the warehouse was destroyed.

enrichments.description:
Image Comics is an American independent comic book publisher and is the third largest direct market comic book and graphic novel publisher in the industry by market share. Its best-known publications include Spawn, The Walking Dead, Kick-Ass, Invincible, Jupiter's Legacy, Witchblade, The Maxx, Savage Dragon, Descender, Saga, East of West, Monstress, Radiant Black, Firebreather, and Stray Dogs.

It was founded in 1992 by several high-profile illustrators as a venue for creator-owned properties, in which comics creators could publish material of their own creation without giving up the copyrights to those properties. Normally this is not the case in the work-for-hire-dominated American comics industry, where the legal author is a publisher, such as Marvel Comics or DC Comics, and the creator is an employee of that publisher. Its output was originally dominated by superhero and fantasy titles from the studios of the founding Image partners, but now includes comics in many genres by numerous independent creators.

enrichments.description:
Amazon MGM Studios is an American film and television production and distribution company and the flagship namesake subsidiary of Amazon. Founded as Amazon Studios on November 16, 2010, the company adopted its current name on October 3, 2023, after its merger with MGM Holdings, which Amazon had acquired the year prior.

Productions from the studio are primarily distributed through theaters and Amazon's own streaming media service, Amazon Prime Video.

Alongside Amazon Prime Video, the company constitutes one half of Amazon's membership in the Motion Picture Association (MPA), which it joined in October 2024.

enrichments.description: Invincible is an American comic book series written by Robert Kirkman, illustrated by Cory Walker and Ryan Ottley, and published by Image Comics. Set in the Image Universe, Invincible follows the coming of age of superhero Mark Grayson / Invincible, a half-Viltrumite and first-born son of Omni-Man, the most powerful superhero on Earth. The series began publication on January 22, 2003, before concluding on February 14, 2018, with 144 issues. Several spin-off series were released over its run: Brit, The Pact, Invincible Presents: Atom Eve & Rex Splode, and Guarding the Globe. An animated television adaptation began streaming on Amazon Prime Video on March 25, 2021, while an additional spin-off interquel, Invincible Universe: Battle Beast, began publication in 2025.

enrichments.description:
Denise Ferguson is a bishop in the Anglican Church of Australia. She served as an assistant bishop in the Anglican Diocese of Adelaide from July 2019, to July 2024 appointed bishop in the Province of South Australia.

Denise was born in New Zealand, and prior to entering ministry served as a staffer to the New Zealand Defence Force. She commenced training for ministry at the age of 39, and began her ministry career in the Anglican Diocese of Wellington, where she was licensed as a lay reader in 1988 and ordained as a deacon in 1999. Ferguson served as vicar of St Matthew's Palmerston North and then as Archdeacon of Manawatu. She later served as the Bishop's Chaplain for Ministry Discernment in the Diocese of Wellington, and her final position prior to relocating to Australia, Ferguson was the Canon Registrar for the Diocese of Waikato and Taranaki.

In 2014 Ferguson moved to Australia, where she worked in the Diocese of Brisbane as Rector of the Parish of East Redland as well as Archdeacon of Moreton.

Ferguson was consecrated as an assistant bishop in the Diocese of Adelaide on 21 July 2019. Her responsibilities involve parish visiting and liturgical roles, as well as oversight of three areas of ministry across South Australia: multicultural diversity in ministry, healthcare chaplaincies – covering both hospital and social service based care contexts – and ministry formation.

Ferguson is married to Martin, an army officer who put his career on hold to support her ministry training. She also has a daughter and is a grandmother.

enrichments.description: Sleepwalker is a fictional character appearing in American comic books published by Marvel Comics. Created by Bob Budiansky and Bret Blevins, he first appeared in Sleepwalker #1 (June 1991). The character is named after his race and is the star of a self-titled comic book which ran for 33 issues, from June 1991 to February 1994, with one Holiday Special. All but two of the issues were written by Budiansky, with Tom Brevoort and Mike Kanterovich writing the Holiday Special and one fill-in issue. Dan Slott also contributed a humorous side story in issue #25.

enrichments.description:
The mayor of Chicago is the  chief executive of city government in Chicago, Illinois, the third-largest city in the United States. The mayor is responsible for the administration and management of various city departments. In addition, the Mayor submits proposals and recommendations to the Chicago City Council, is active in the enforcement of the city's ordinances, submits the city's annual budget and appoints city officers, department commissioners or directors, and members of city boards and commissions.

During sessions of the city council, the mayor serves as the presiding officer. The mayor is not allowed to vote on issues except in certain instances, most notably where the vote taken on a matter before the body results in a tie.

The office of mayor was created when Chicago became a city in 1837.

Agent Spider is a minor character in Invincible, debuting in Season 2.

He is an spider-themed superhero that hails from another universe in which Invincible meets after Angstrom Levy sends him through the multiverse.

Agent Spider has a black bodysuit covered in webs, with dijon yellow colored clothing padding on his arms and legs, and spider like web designs for his torso and chest, his chest has a big letter of silver colored A, standing for “Agent", he has red lenses, and is covered in a antique white colored full mask. He also wears a grey utility belt and vest where his logo is placed along with grey tactical boots and pair of gloves matching colors of his mask with exception of three fingers each colored black.

Agent Spider is depicted as a carefree but compassionate person brimming with experience, willing to assist even a total stranger during their moments of need. Despite his enigmatic presence, he displays full a his sense of humor which often annoys his opponents and his allies at the same time.

She is a vibrant cyan-blue insectoid creature resembling a mantis, with two multifaceted red eyes and a pair of antennae. Her arms are lined with long spines, and her hands have two fingers each. Her forelegs end with two toes.

As a Thraxan, Andressa lives quite a short life from a human point of view. At a young age, she was very wise and forgiving as is with most Thraxans as shown when she says, "Thraxans forgive and move on." She was always quick to fall in love, which is shown in her short relationship with Nolan (Omni-Man). She falls madly in love with him very quickly. She still misses Nolan even after he was taken by the other not-so-friendly Viltrumites, which is why in her dying moments she gave their son Oliver to Mark, so as to protect him from the evil Viltrum Empire, as well as to give him a place with a family to look after him.

entities.description:
Queen Aquaria is a minor character in Invincible. She was the wife of King Aquarus, the King of Atlantis and a former member of the Guardians of the Globe.

Aquaria appears as an anthropomorphic fish with a humanoid body. She possesses fins extending from her head and back, webbed arms and legs, and light blue skin.

She wears a flowing dark blue gown with matching armor-like shoulder pieces and a golden tiara adorned with a purple gemstone at its centre.

Unlike her late husband, Aquarus, Queen Aquaria takes her royal duties very seriously and places the welfare of Atlantis above the concerns of the surface world. Following Aquarus’s death, she upholds Atlantean law by holding Invincible, as Nolan’s next of kin, accountable for the king’s murder. Despite her stern and authoritative demeanor, she is pragmatic rather than cruel, having abolished the kingdom’s former marriage custom as barbaric. After Invincible risks his life to save both her and her people from the Depth-Dweller, she considers Aquarus’s death atoned for and ends the matter.

entities.description:

King Aquarus was a hydrokinetic creature from an undersea nation and an original member of the Guardians of the Globe. He had worked with Omni-Man but was betrayed and murdered by him.

Aquarus, as all other Atlanteans, appears as an anthropomorphic fish, sporting fins growing out from his back and arms. His skin color is also predominantly blue. He would only usually wear what seemed to be a piece of Atlantean equipment as clothing, the armor would be a mix of green and white with yellow outlines surrounding it. Like all the other Guardians, Aquarus wore a piece of equipment resembling a wristband that would signal an alert anytime him or any of the other Guardians were needed in action.

Aquarus seemed to only be in the Guardians as a way to have some fun, seen from his excitement of getting an alert from Guardians HQ. He would also be mostly neglectful of his people, usually busy with Guardians business while his wife would continue to rule the kingdom. Despite his flaws, he still was a good person, caring deeply for his comrades, being in shock after seeing what Omni-Man had done to his friends.

entities.description:
Argall is the overarching antagonist of Invincible, debuting in Season 4's flashbacks. He is the late mentor of his former protégé, Thragg.

He was the first, and remains the most revered Emperor of the Viltrum Empire; his reign is considered to be the Golden Age of Viltrum. He was murdered by Thaedus, the first Viltrumite to betray the Empire. Nearly a thousand years later, Argall would be avenged by his regent successor, Thragg, who killed Thaedus in the climax of the Viltrumite War.

Argall was an older Viltrumite with a similar build to Thaedus. He was muscular, with a traditional white mustache and a balding head, with white hair along the sides. Following his assassination, his skull was left fractured at the crown where Thaedus struck him. His regent successor, Thragg, later kept the skull as a reminder of his duty to the Empire.

Argall's imperial attire consisted of a crimson ceremonial cloak trimmed with a large white fur mantle, worn over a crimson-and-gray Viltrumite uniform bearing a gray Viltrum Empire emblem on the chest. The lower half of the uniform was covered by a gray skirt.

Arthur "Art" Rosenbaum is supporting character in Invincible, debuting from Season 1 and onwards.

He is a tailor who creates suits and designs costumes worn by heroes. He also creates garments since the public is unaware of his costume side project. Art created a costume for Omni-Man upon their initial meeting and subsequently designed one for Nolan's son, Invincible.

Art has graying hair, which is slightly messy. His hair is short and a bit unkempt with a receding hairline. Art has a round face with a friendly, laid-back expression. As a tailor, Art wears simple work clothes, including a greenish-brownish shirt and slacks, often with an apron when he’s at work. His clothing is practical and not flashy, fitting with his no-nonsense, hands-on approach to his craft. His face is lined with age, and he’s often seen with a warm, welcoming smile.

In a flashback, when Art was younger, he is shown to have brown hair with grey sides, a hairstyle similar to Nolan. He wears a grey shirt with black formal trousers and black shoes and little to no wrinkles and a more leaner physique.

Nolan fought fiercely against the monster, and his fight caught the attention of the GDA who discovered the two, Nolan had then cut the beast in half as his blood was covered all over Nolan's uniform by the time Cecil arrived.

Following the deaths of Scott's sister and niece, Becky fostered a profound sense of animosity in Scott and helped him in his vengeful crusade against Invincible. Best Tiger is a minor character in Invincible, debuting from Season 3 and onwards.

He is a gunfighter/martial-artist superhero.

Best Tiger's info and origins are entirely unknown, but he was born in Hong Kong, China, and is a master ninja alongside a master marksman/gunman. While having perfect vision, he wears a blindfold as a self-imposed challenge to make fights more difficult, not because he needs it.

Best Tiger had discovered Capevincible had invaded Hong Kong; who greeted him rather cheerfully. Managing to evade him, Tiger then used the infrastructure around him to ricochet a shot that surprisingly sent Capevincible flying back.

entities.name: Betsy Wilkins
entities.description:
Elizabeth "Betsy" Wilkins is a supporting character in Invincible, debuting from Season 1 and onwards. She is the wife of Adam Wilkins, and the adoptive mother of Samantha Eve Wilkins.

Betsy is a middle aged, fair skinned woman with brown hair. Her hair is cut at a medium length and is parted to both sides of her head from the top.

She is seen wearing a pink shirt that has a white stripe near the top, separating the deep pink section of the shirt and the pale pink section around her neck and shoulders. Along with this shirt, she wears a light grey overshirt. On her left wrist she wears a green bracelet as well as a necklace around her neck which appears to have a bronze leaf at the end. To complete her outfit she wears a pair of yellow shoes.

Betsy is often shown to be far more reasonable than her husband. Despite this, she believes her daughter's superhero life is too risky, particularly if she's not being protected by other superheroes like her former boyfriend Rex Splode. Even when Eve was young, Betsy was less focused on what others thought and more concerned over her daughter's wellbeing as she wanted to give Eve the best life she could possibly deliver as her mother.

entities.name: Bi-Plane
entities.description:
Bi-Plane was a notorious winged criminal in Denver, known for robbing banks using his flying contraption. Eventually, he discovered that he had contracted cancer and decided to lace himself with plutonium, planning to blow himself up above the city, which would have made the entire area radioactive. Fortunately for the residents, The Immortal arrived on the scene, quickly apprehended Bi-Plane, and threw him into space, killing him instantly. Later, Invincible encounters Bi-Plane's corpse in space during his trip to Mars.

Bi-Plane is a slender, bald man with pale skin. He wears a green jumpsuit that has lighter green sections on the limbs, complemented by a brown harness and boots. His most distinctive feature is the large jet pack he wears, which resembles a combination of a jet turbine and the wings of an airplane.

What little is seen of Bi-Plane shows that he is a maniacal, genocidal, and suicidal. Not only was he willing to kill himself, but an entire city with plutonium explosives that he had lined into his suit. Bi-Plane also appears to be boastful, arrogant, cocky, and absent-minded. He ran on with his monologue and did not even bother to pay attention to the Immortal who wasted no time in neutralizing him.

entities.description:
Markus Grimshaw, also known as Black Samson, is a supporting character in Invincible, debuting from Season 1 and onwards.

He is a member of the Guardians of the Globe. He was once part of the Guardians original roster until he lost his powers and left the team. He would later rejoin the team under Robot’s command.

In his youth, Black Samson was already a tall and exceptionally muscular man, possessing a broad chest, thick arms, wide shoulders, and a powerful athletic build. He had dark skin, short black hair, and a relatively smooth, youthful face. Even at this stage of his career, his physique was notably bulky and imposing.

As an older man, Black Samson retains his tall, heavily muscular physique, with broad shoulders, a large chest, thick arms, and a powerful overall build. He is bald and has a more mature appearance, with prominent facial lines around his eyes, cheeks, and mouth. His facial features are strong and angular, including a broad nose, pronounced cheekbones, and a defined jaw.

entities.name: Bryant
entities.description:
Bryant was a minor character who briefly appeared in first season. He was a member of a group that worshipped an ancient being known as Ka-Hor, and he sought to unearth his tomb in order to free him from his centuries long imprisonment.

Upon unearthing Ka-Hor’s tomb and awakening him, Bryant was possessed by Ka-Hor due to a curse that required him to inhabit a living host in order to escape. Before Ka-Hor could escape, however, a sandstorm inadvertently caused by Invincible sealed the tomb once more and trapped both of them inside. Bryant eventually died after being trapped for so long, leaving Ka-Hor without a host.

Bryant also had a daughter named Jane who, together with another woman and minor superhuman named Riley, eventually rediscovered the tomb, where she found the desiccated remains of her father before encountering Ka-Hor.

He was an American/Australian male with dark brown hair and a peach-fuzz beard. He was seen wearing a yellow jacket, green shirt, khaki pants, and a white scarf. He was shown smoking and was notable for having a scarab beetle tattoo on his right hand, signifying his devotion to Ka-Hor.

entities.name: Caitlin Stedman
entities.description:
Caitlin Stedman is a variant of Cecil Stedman from another universe, with the primary distinction being her gender. She acts as a minor character in Season 2.

Little is known about Caitlin's backstory, though it is suggested to be very similar to the mainstream Cecil. She eventually rose to the rank of director within the Global Defense Agency with Denise as her second in command. During her tenure, she and the GDA uncovered the betrayal of both Omni-Man and Invincible. They succeeded in killing Omni-Man and later captured Invincible, imprisoning him. Sometime after his incarceration, Caitlin and Denise witnessed a mysterious individual speaking with the imprisoned Invincible before disappearing through a portal.

This female variant of Cecil Stedman is an older woman with pale, weathered skin and sharp, angular facial features. Her silver hair is styled in a neat, voluminous wave, adding to her authoritative presence. Deep lines and a large scar on her face, giving her a hardened, battle-worn appearance. She wears a light-colored blazer over a dark collared shirt, complete with a U.S. flag pin on her chest. Her look is completed by bold red earrings, and her cold, calculating gaze reflects a lifetime of leadership, strategy, and ruthless decision-making.

Caitlin Stedman is calm, pragmatic, and unwavering in her leadership of the Global Defense Agency in her universe, similar to that of her male original counterpart. Sharp-minded and unafraid to confront danger head-on, she maintains a collected presence in unpredictable situations. Though her screen time is brief, her decisive tone and commanding demeanour speak volumes. When she and her colleague Denise discover a mysterious figure, Angstrom, speaking to the imprisoned Invincible, Caitlin doesn’t hesitate to challenge him: “Who the hell are you?” Her sharp interrogation reveals a leader who doesn’t tolerate surprises and is always ready to take control.

One day, a portal from another dimension opened up, with it the arrival of another superhero from that world, Invincible. The two have a conversation about his name's originality. Despite this little argument, it is implied that the Vigilante helped the inter-dimensional hero find another portal to return to his reality.

The Cruise Kaiju is a massive, serpentine leviathan with a menacing, alien presence. entities.name: D.A. Sinclair
entities.description:
D.A. Sinclair is a minor character in Invincible. He initially debuted as a minor antagonist in Season 1, before beginning to redeem himself from Season 2 and onwards.

He is a genius who attended Upstate University thanks to a special program he was awarded. He believes that any weakness a human has is an obstacle to be solved by engineering. After being taken down by Invincible when caught manipulating humans and turning them into ReAnimen, he was hired by Cecil Stedman to create an army of them that could repel any incoming Viltrumite invasion. Unlike his original ReAnimen, the new ones he created while working for Cecil were made using corpses instead of living people.

Sinclair is a lean, young male of average height with pale light skin. He keeps his black hair at neck length and slicked back, with a noticeable widow's peak. He has greyish-blue eyes, an aquiline nose, and a sharp chin. After his first encounter with Invincible, Sinclair's jaw was dislocated and his nose was broken. By the time Cecil recruited him to build ReAnimen in order to counter the Viltrumites, he was outfitted with a neck brace. Sinclair had a swollen mandible and left cheek, a swollen nose, and a black eye on the left side. In this condition, he was unable to speak, instead grunting and emitting muffled sounds. His injuries had fully healed after at least a month following the fight between Invincible and Omni-Man.

Sinclair dresses in greyish-mauve business clothes, consisting of a suit jacket, a mauve tie, trousers, and laced shoes. He wears a white undershirt beneath the jacket. While performing surgery in his underground laboratory, he wore a lab apron, plastic gloves, and a doctor's cap over his civilian attire. While operating in the GDA laboratories, his surgical clothes included a white lab jacket, a blue undershirt with a high collar and hood, blue gloves, and a pair of yellow goggles.

entities.name: Damien Darkblood
entities.description:
Damien Darkblood is a supporting character in Invincible, debuting from Season 1 and onwards.

He is a demon detective who pursues justice from others to redeem his own soul and repay a debt. He had worked for the Global Defense Agency and investigated the deaths of the Guardians of the Globe before he was returned to Hell for refusing the cease the investigation as ordered by Cecil Stedman. Following his exile, Damien soon reunited with his family in Hell and put himself in the service of its former ruler, Satan.

When a dangerous threat known as Volcanikka emerged in Hell and threatened to destroy both it as well as the surface world, Damien and his family worked tirelessly with Satan to stop her. However, they were unable to match her overwhelming strength, so Damien aimed to summon Omni-Man to Hell to enlist his services in stopping Volcanikka. Unaware that he had long since left the planet, Damien inadvertently summoned Omni-Man's son, Invincible, instead. Together, they stopped Volcanikka and returned Satan to power in Hell.

Damien was then allowed by Satan to return to the surface world with Invincible, having repaid his debt in-full. Upon his return, Damien was also tasked by Satan to investigate and figure out why Volcanikka aimed to conquer the surface world in the first place.

entities.description:
Daphne is one of the minor characters in Invincible, debuting from Season 3 and onwards. She is the girlfriend of D.A. Sinclair.

Daphne is a female human, with pink-shirt and a pink business-skirt with a tie. She wears glasses and her hair is black. Daphne also wears a lab white jacket.

Daphne is shown in her dialogue, to be a cold scientist, sounding somewhat devoid of humanity, almost mirroring to her boyfriend who wanted remove humanity in some matter.

Little much is known about her backstory, at some point, Daphne ended up working with the G.D.A and eventually met her love interest, D.A. Sinclair.

Benjamin Taylor, formerly known as Nightboy, is supporting character in Invincible, debuting from Season 2 to 3. Initially serving as a minor antagonist since his debut, he begins to redeem himself in Season 3 and onward. He is the original Darkwing's protégé. Following his mentor's death, Benjamin inherited the Darkwing mantle and attempted to continue his predecessor's crusade against crime.

However, unlike the original Darkwing, Benjamin's methods became dramatically more violent. His paranoia, distrust, and willingness to murder anyone he perceived as a criminal eventually pushed him into a psychological breakdown. He became increasingly delusional, developing a distorted perception of himself as a heroic figure despite committing numerous atrocities.

His encounter with Invincible ultimately resulted in his capture and subsequent rehabilitation under Cecil Stedman and the Global Defense Agency. After confronting the consequences of his actions, Benjamin began attempting to redeem himself and became a member of both the G.D.A. and the Guardians of the Globe.

The Data Twins are members of the Coalition of Planets responsible for analyzing their data.

The twins are grey humanoid aliens, one is thin, the second is overweight, both have enlarged heads, and are supplied to a blue wire when sitting on chairs, they wear blue short shirts and shorts.

The twins exhibit a certain level of arrogance, as they would reprimand Coalition agents for errors made during their missions.

The twins have spent years with the Coalition of Planets, demonstrating unwavering commitment to the mission of stopping the Viltrum Empire's efforts for good. They oversee the data records of all Coalition agents.

entities.description:

Markus Sebastian "Mark" Grayson, better known as Defeated Invincible, is an evil variant of the main Invincible and a minor antagonist in the second season of Invincible.

Like many alternate versions of Mark, he accepted his father Nolan Grayson's offer to join the Viltrumite Empire, helping him wage war across Earth. Unlike most of his counterparts, however, he failed to conquer the planet. Global military forces eventually defeated both him and Omni-Man. Nolan was killed by experimental quantum bombs that devastated much of Europe, while Mark was gradually worn down by the combined resistance. Once exhaustion finally forced him to sleep, the Global Defense Agency seized the opportunity to capture him and imprison him in one of its highest-security facilities.

At some point, this variant of Invincible was visited by a multiverse hopping Angstrom who was seeking revenge on the mainstream Invincible. Angstrom promised the variant he would free him if he gave him information, though he quickly went back on it and left the variant in his prison.

Demi-God appears as a floating purple head which seems to be his entire body, or a form of it. He wears a gray sweater vest over a white shirt with a blue tie and black gloves along with gray pants and brown shoes.

Demi-God wields a metal staff with a floating purple orb at the tip.

Demi-God was one of the many superheroes present during tryouts for the Guardians of the Globe, though he was not one of the heroes selected to join the new group in the end.

entities.name: Denise Ferguson
entities.description:
Denise Ferguson is a bishop in the Anglican Church of Australia. She served as an assistant bishop in the Anglican Diocese of Adelaide from July 2019, to July 2024 appointed bishop in the Province of South Australia.

Denise was born in New Zealand, and prior to entering ministry served as a staffer to the New Zealand Defence Force. She commenced training for ministry at the age of 39, and began her ministry career in the Anglican Diocese of Wellington, where she was licensed as a lay reader in 1988 and ordained as a deacon in 1999. Ferguson served as vicar of St Matthew's Palmerston North and then as Archdeacon of Manawatu. She later served as the Bishop's Chaplain for Ministry Discernment in the Diocese of Wellington, and her final position prior to relocating to Australia, Ferguson was the Canon Registrar for the Diocese of Waikato and Taranaki.

In 2014 Ferguson moved to Australia, where she worked in the Diocese of Brisbane as Rector of the Parish of East Redland as well as Archdeacon of Moreton.

Ferguson was consecrated as an assistant bishop in the Diocese of Adelaide on 21 July 2019. Her responsibilities involve parish visiting and liturgical roles, as well as oversight of three areas of ministry across South Australia: multicultural diversity in ministry, healthcare chaplaincies – covering both hospital and social service based care contexts – and ministry formation.

Ferguson is married to Martin, an army officer who put his career on hold to support her ministry training. She also has a daughter and is a grandmother.

The Depth Dweller is a minor antagonist in Invincible, debuting in Season 2.

She is a kaiju (giant sea monster) that is held captive in a trench in Atlantis, which the Atlantean Queen Aquaria used in a failed attempt to execute Invincible, as retribution for Invincible's father murdering Aquaria's husband and predecessor King Aquarus.

The length of time the Depth Dweller was chained by the queen remains unknown, as it is possible that the chaining occurred either during the period when the King became a superhero or at another time altogether. The queen, having assumed greater control over the kingdom than her husband, has made the decision to employ this creature as a means of punishment instead of utilizing marriage.

entities.description:
David Anders, better known as Dinosaurus, is a major antagonist in Invincible, debuting from Season 4 and onwards.

He is a brilliant but mentally unstable human scientist who harbours a dissociative alter ego, transforming him into a powerful, red, humanoid dinosaur when his other persona takes control. As a radical utilitarian and lethal ecoterrorist, he believes that humanity can only survive and prosper if certain individuals are eliminated, justifying mass destruction as necessary for the greater good.

David Anders is a scrawny, ordinary-looking man.

Dinosaurus has a muscular, humanoid build with red skin, yellow eyes, and a long tail. His hands and feet have sharp claws capable of tearing through enemies, while his large, sharp yellow teeth and prominent crest give him a distinctly dinosaur-like appearance. Despite his humanoid physique, he closely resembles a Tyrannosaurus. Dinosaurus wears brown pants and armor covering his lower legs, shoulders, and tail.

Doc Seismic is a recurring antagonist in Invincible, debuting from Season 1 and onwards.

He is a radical seismologist who holds a profound disdain for contemporary society, perceiving it as characterized by oppression. He seemingly seeks to advance his political aims by dismantling American monuments and restoring the Earth to its original state.

Doc Seismic is an older man with a mostly bald head save for a few small strands of hair. His eyebrows are dark and sharp, and he has deeply lined features that show his age. His build is lean rather than muscular, and his posture gives him an air of intensity.

entities.name: Doug Cheston
entities.description:
Doug Cheston is a minor character in Invincible, debuting in Season 1.

He was son of the owner of Cheston Pharmaceutical and half the Upstate University. He was kidnapped and transformed into a ReAnimen by D.A. Sinclair. He eventually escaped Sinclair's lab and went on a rampage across the college, fighting Invincible before committing suicide.

Three girls Doug approaches while drunk realize his father had elevated prices on a medicine, but he tells them that he would inherit everything soon, offering them sex, but they refuse. He is attacked from behind and is put to sleep.thumb|left|200px|ReAniman Doug choking William.

When Doug awakens, D.A. Sinclair tells him that he would be turned into a brave explorer. Doug calls him a nerd, but he finds he is bound and trapped in a basement with multiple cyborgs. He looks at his arm, which is now partially robotic, which surprises him. Since he did not stay quiet, D.A. Sinclair cuts his throat open and removes his vocal chords.thumb|200px|The aftermath of Doug and Invincible's fight.|left

entities.description:
Download is a humanoid alien with a lean built, with grey skin and hair. His eyes are fully blue, appear to lack pupils entirely.

Download wears a standard Coalitions Officer Uniform mostly identical to that of Captain Pikell. He wears a full-sleeve, collared up shirt with a black and yellow colour design and an Emblem. He also wears black pants with a silver metallic belt and black shoes.

Little is known about Download personality, but he appears to be a diligent man devoted to his work, following his captain's orders and trying to keep the crumbling Venture together, as shown when the group enters an asteroid field and he gets disappointed at not being able to fix the ship.

Despite following Captain Pikell's reckneless order to destroy the Rognarr planet's disc, he votes alongside the other crew members to replace him for the more competent General Telia.

He and his brother are members of the Rebellion, dedicated to their mission of stopping the king. They traveled to the past and convinced Invincible to overthrow the king's reign.

Much like his brother, he has a tanned complexion and a muscular build. He has long, dark brown hair and similarly colored dark brown eyes.

He wears a fitted purple uniform with long sleeves and light gray armor on his shoulders and knees. A beige utility belt with attached pouches wraps around his waist, and his gloves are beige with exposed fingers. He has gray knee guards strapped over long white leggings that are tucked into purple shoes that match his outfit.

entities.name: Ed Thompson
entities.description:
Ed Thompson is a minor character in Invincible, debuting in Season 4. He is the father of Zoe Thompson.

Ed Thompson is an overweight Caucasian man with light brown hair, a beard, and a well-groomed haircut. He also has brown eyes.

Ed Thompson is a compassionate, kind and very involved father who loves his daughter Zoe very much. He operates with a laid-back, funny side, but he is not without setting rules and asking his daughter to behave, for instance, he does not hesitate to scold her for cursing. Instead of being strictly disciplinary he is quite lenient and understanding, usually when Zoe makes mistakes he reminds her in a kind way rather than punishing her with severity.

He is very confident in Zoe's capability to make right decisions and he honors her being independent. When she is asked to join the Coalition of Planets in the fight against the Viltrumites, he does not try to stop her despite the immense danger involved. Instead, he supports her decision, believing it is the right thing to do, while making sure she knows she has his full encouragement.

entities.description:
El Chupacabra is a minor character in Invincible. He is one of the many superheroes who participated in the Invincible War, fighting alongside others in the global effort to stop the evil Invincible variants.

El Chupacabra wears a distinctive jungle green and burnt orange costume with a fierce, primal design. The majority of the outfit is green, while burnt orange accents cover the eye mask, portions of the gloves, shoulders, and the emblem on his chest. His gloves and leggings are primarily white, providing contrast to the darker tones. His costume is adorned with numerous spikes, most notably on his mask, arms, shoulder blades, and elongated clawed gloves, enhancing his fierce, beast-like appearance.

El Chupacabra is known for his fearlessness, demonstrated when he boldly faced off against a powerful variant of Invincible during the Invincible War.

Little is known about El Chupacabra’s background, other than his real name, Francisco Vasquez, and that he was hired by the Global Defense Agency.

Elia is a minor Coalition representative in Invincible debuting in Season 4.

At some point, Elia joined the Coalition of Planets in fear of Viltrumites to seek protection from them. She eventually became a Coalition Representative and appeared through various of meetings about what to do with Viltrumites. After Thaedus' death, Allen became new leader of the Coalition, which made Elia unhappy as she seems to not trust Allen with his new job.

Elia is a representative within the Coalition of Planets, though little is known about her past.

Elia appears among with other Coalition representatives during a meeting regarding the Viltrum Empire with Thaedus.

entities.name: Elias Brandyworth
entities.description:
Dr. Elias Brandyworth was a government scientist, assistant director of the Pentagon's department of superhuman research and Atom Eve's creator.

In his initial appearance, Elias Brandyworth has White/gray hair which is fairly long and well combed. He wears a pink shirt, brown pants and blue sport shoes along with a long white lab coat while working as a scientist for the government. After going rogue, Brandyworth has essentially become homeless, spotting a dirty brown coat over his lab attire, his hair has grown longer and more shaggy, he has also grown a full beard and wrinkles, making him look tired and much older than he should look.

Elias Brandyworth was an intelligent man who was extremely dedicated to his work and passionate about breaking new grounds in genetic engineering. After meeting Polly, he forms a deep friendship with her, keeping a close watch on her at all times during her pregnancy. During this time, Brandyworth had a change of heart and realized the error in his line of work and went out of his way to save Polly and her unborn child from being turned into Government experiments.

After Polly's death and him being fired by the Pentagon, Brandyworth becomes homeless, spending his days closely monitoring on Eve from the shadows and trying to reconnect with her. He became extremely protective of Eve. Instructing her to not use her powers to not cause any attention her way, but after realising that Eve was now a hero in the making, Brandyworth instead chose to give her closure about her past and how much he wished for her to have a normal life.

The Elite Guard is a minor character in Season 3 of Invincible. He is seen stopping Multi-Paul's escape attempt from Payton Penitentiary in Episode 5.

The guard wears a heavily armored plated vest along with arm guards and leg guards of a similar strength. He wears a helmet with a gas mask or mouth guard and a black balaclava underneath his headwear. Under his armor he wears a grey jumpsuit with a black belt, he also wears black gloves and boots. His armor has pockets and holsters, likely for storing ammo, weaponry, or equipment.

He is seen to be brute like in behavior, likely because of his training to deal with super powered prisoners in Payton Penitentiary.

Nothing is known of his backstory, except for the fact he became an Elite Guard in the Payton Penitentiary.

She is a ruthless Viltrumite warrior of the Viltrum Empire, committed to its mission of universal domination. Following Viltrum's destruction, Elix resettled into Earth's human society to find suitable mates to interbreed with and repopulate the Empire.

Elix is a lanky woman with light skin, cold light-blue eyes, and semi-short white hair. She has a slim build, with prominent cheekbones.

Like most other Viltrumites, Elix wears the standard Viltrumite uniform.

entities.description:
Beatrice Washington, also know as Ella Mental is an original character created by Robert Kirkman for Invincible VS. She made her comic debut in May 2026 in a backup story of issue 7-12 of Capes by Kirkman and Cory Walker.

The heiress to her family’s fortune, Ella’s studious and hardworking nature earned her the spot as her grandfather’s favorite. Soon, she was entrusted with access to an ancient totem—one which gave her the power to control the four elements. Full of energy and determination, Ella set out on a new journey, becoming the superhero Ella Mental.

Ella Mental is a female African American superhero with brown hair and orange-red eyes, similar to lava. She sports a green superhero costume consisting of a sleeveless suit with gold adornments, fingerless gloves, and a cape.

Despite her immense powers and only recently obtaining them, Ella is shown to be very humble and selfless. Very cautious, she carefully considered what kind of person she wanted to be to help the world with her powers.

Embrace is a supporting villain who first appears in Season 3 of Invincible.

Embrace wears a sleek red suit that leaves her shoulders bare, adorned with gold accents scattered throughout. She complements her look with gold earrings and various other golden accessories, adding a touch of elegance to her villainous appearance.

Embrace appears to be calm, composed, and calculating. Her silence during Machine Head’s return suggests she’s either cautious or respectful of authority, preferring to observe and assess before acting. This restraint may indicate a strategic mind, someone who weighs her options carefully rather than acting impulsively. Her stylish and refined outfit, paired with her golden accessories, also hints at a level of vanity or elegance, suggesting she values appearance and presentation. While little is known of her true intentions, her presence among a council of villains implies a dangerous capability masked behind her quiet demeanor.

Much like most versions of Invincible, he accepted his dad's offer in joining the Viltrumite empire, causing havoc across the entire world.

Executioner Invincible has black hair with a widows-peak that is combed back with a few strands sticking up, and brown eyes.

Executioner Invincible’s hair sticks out of the top of his suit which has a yellow mask with goggles. The suit is yellow down the middle, stopping at his waist in an upside-down triangle shape, it also bears blue on the shoulders and going into the yellow in somewhat of an M shape. The rest of his costume is black aside from the yellow gloves and blue boots that start from his knee's down.

Almost nothing is known about this version of Invincible, except for the fact that he became a supervillain in his reality.

The face wears a brown mask with three lenses to look through, along with a green shirt, a backpack, and gloves.

After the “death” of Mister Liu from the hands of Machine Head, The Face was with other members of The Order waiting for their leader only to learn that he is dead and Machine Head is taking his spot as their leader. Titan came in during Machine Head's speech with information that he only wants his city while The Order can take the rest of the world, but he is leaving the group.

entities.name: Fightmaster
entities.description:
Fightmaster is one of two minor characters in Invincible, debuting in Season 3. He is the twin brother of Dropkick.

He and his brother are members of the Rebellion, dedicated to their mission of stopping the king. They traveled to the past and convinced Invincible to overthrow the king's reign.

Fightmaster appears to be a moderately tanned human male with a muscular build. He has dark brown eyes and long hair of a similar color. Sideburns go down the sides of his face.

He wears a sleeveless yellow jacket over a fitted orange outfit with a white panel down the chest. His shorts are orange and reach just above the knees, and he has gray knee guards strapped over long white leggings. His gloves are beige with open fingers, and his shoes are orange with thick soles.
entities.short_description: Fightmaster is one of two minor characters in Invincible, debuting in Season 3. He is the twin brother of Dropkick.

entities.name: Filip Schaff
entities.description:
Filip Schaff is a fictional comic book creator in Invincible, first appearing in Season 2. He is best known as the creator of the popular in-universe comic character Seance Dog, a supernatural canine wizard who has gained a dedicated following.

Filip Schaff is of average height with a slightly stocky, broad-shouldered build. He has a neatly groomed dark brown beard and mustache, and his dark brown hair is mostly hidden beneath a navy blue baseball cap. He has a light skin tone and wears a gray zip-up hoodie over a light gray collared shirt. Around his neck is a red lanyard with an ID badge, likely for Comic Coon entry.

Filip Schaff is a friendly and approachable comic book creator with a deep passion for his craft. When meeting Mark, Filip comes across as genuinely humble and grateful, warmly responding to Mark’s admiration by signing his book and engaging in casual conversation.

During their chat, Filip reveals his passion and deep knowledge of animation, explaining the long production times and the clever shortcuts animators use, like hiding characters’ mouths or using distant wide shots to mask limited movement. His playful humor shines through as he jokes about these tricks, making the complex process sound fun and relatable.

entities.name: Fiona
entities.description:
Fiona is a minor character in Invincible, debuting from Season 1 and onwards. She is the daughter of Titan and Vanessa.

Fiona appears as a young African-American girl. She has braided pigtails with orange beads.

Fiona is portrayed as a compassionate, happy-go-lucky young girl who loves her parents deeply. Despite finally enjoying an improved life due to her father, she remained true to her authentic self and never let her newfound status show to others.

Fiona was born to Titan and Vanessa. From a very young age, she's been struggling with a physical ailment, to which she manages with specific medications.

entities.name: Flaxan Leader
entities.description:
The Flaxan Leader was a prominent figure among the alien Flaxan race, initially appearing as just another soldier during their first invasion of Earth. However, after surviving that failed assault and receiving a disfiguring scar from Invincible, he rose through the ranks to become the leader of the second and third Flaxan invasions.

Fueled by vengeance and a desire to conquer Earth, he quickly became one of Invincible’s most persistent and personal adversaries. His reign of terror came to a violent end when Omni-Man followed the Flaxans through their portal into their home dimension and singlehandedly annihilated their civilization, brutally killing the Flaxan Leader in the process.

The Flaxan Leader was a green-skinned alien distinguished by six antennae and striking black eyes with yellow, vertical pupils.

During the first invasion, he appeared as a standard soldier, clad in a blue jumpsuit complemented by white armor. This armor included a chest plate, pelvic guard, shoulder and knee pads, and sturdy boots, functional and uniform in design.

entities.name: Flyby Invincible
entities.description:
Markus Sebastian "Mark" Grayson, better known as Invincible, is a evil version of the main Invincible from an alternate universe and a minor antagonist in the second season of Invincible. Much like most versions of Invincible, he accepted his dad's offer in joining the Viltrum Empire, causing havoc across the entire world.

Flyby Invincible has black hair with a widows-peak that is combed back with a few strands sticking up, and brown eyes.

Flyby Invincible’s hair sticks out of the top of his suit which has a yellow mask with goggles. The suit is yellow down the middle, stopping at his waist in an upside-down triangle shape, it also bears blue on the shoulders and going into the yellow in somewhat of an M shape. The rest of his costume is black aside from the yellow gloves and blue boots that start from his knee's down.

Nothing is known about this version of Invincible.

entities.name: Force Fist
entities.description:
Force Fist is one of the minor antagonists in Invincible. He, along with his wife Knuckle Buster, made up the Order of The Freeing Fist and were enemies of Cecil Stedman. The duo operated as terrorists seeking to tear down modern society and end industrialization.

Force Fist was a tall adult man with light skin, sandy-blond hair reaching down to his nape and blue eyes. He had a muscular, mid-weight physique, with pronounced abdominal and pectoral muscles. His wardrobe consisted of a dark blue leotard with elbow length sleeves, a V-line extending to his naval region and leg covering extended just above his heels. He also sported a red bandana, concealing his forehead and scalp, but with an opening for his hair. Finishing his costume were a pair of red fingerless gloves, red boots, a red sash and a black strap around his right thigh. The Order of the Freeing Fist emblem, a white winged skull, was located on his chest.

Force Fist was a fanatical humanist extremist who opposed industrial life. Both him and his wife proved to be delusional, believing that through mass murder and chaos humanity would relinquish modern society for a more optimal way of life. To that end, the two attempted to release a flesh killing bio-weapon upon a city, in hopes that others would learn from their example. As the gas began to peel away at their skin, neither of them seemed to mind the pain but rather accepted it, highlighting their resolve.

After having his body refitted with new skin, Force Fist had been recruited into the GDA. Radcliffe believed that he and Knuckle Buster had been fully rehabilitated while under his supervision, willing to help the GDA with its operations. This turnover was never fully explored, however, given the pair had been shot to death before they could demonstrate any sincerity.

His full body armour is a brown robotic suit with his torso being circular and combined with the head piece. it has orange grid line eye pieces and highlights, with dual flamethrowers on each hand and a canon on the back. Underneath the suit he is a humanoid mass of plasma.

Little known about his backstory, he is composed of plasma and eventually became a supervillain, donning a full suit of battle armor.
