entities.description:
Gary is a minor character, who briefly appears in Season 1.

Gary has a receding hairline, which makes him look a bit older or stressed. He appears to be light-skinned, though the exact tone isn’t super distinct. His outfit suggests he might be a low-level businessman or a office worker.

He seems to be a good caring father to his daughter.

Gary owed a debt to Machine Head who sent Titan to kill him but the latter discovers that Gary has a family, so he gives Gary the opportunity to settle the bill within two days. He may have settled the bill afterwards.

entities.name: Gecko
entities.description:
Gecko is a minor antagonist in Invincible, debuting in Atom Eve's backstory.

Gecko is one of the members of the Lizard League who participated the battle between them and the Guardians. His current status and whereabouts is unknown.

Little is known about his backstory. At some point, he joined the Lizard League.

In 2004, he and the other Lizard League members, along with the queen and the prince, raided the facility. When the Guardians of the Globe appeared, they engaged in battle, with Gecko seen dodging Aquarus’s attacks. Gecko began clutching his throat while struggling to breathe before Aquarus attacked him again, but he managed to dodge it once more. He was ultimately knocked out by War Woman.

entities.description:
The Gelderian emperor is a minor character in Invincible, debuting from Season 2 and onwards.

He is a member of the Coalition of Planets and the sovereign ruler of Gelderia.

Little is known of the Gelderian emperor, except he is the leader of Gelderia, and is a member of the Coalition of Planets after his people and his home is being attacked by the Viltrum Empire. The Emperor was seen upon learning from Allen of the Viltrumite-Human hybrid known as Invincible. Like everyone else, he was against the idea of trusting the young hybrid, but Thaedus supported Allen's theory that Invincible might be the key to helping them end the war against the Viltrumites once and for all.

entities.name: Giant
entities.description:
The Giant is a recurring character in Invincible, appearing as a one-time antagonist in Season 2 and a minor character in Season 3.

The Giant is a colossal cyclops. He has one eye, which makes him cycloptic, and he seems to have an underbite with two lower teeth that are bigger than the rest. He sports black fingerless gloves adorned with silver bands and knuckles along with black pants featuring a silver waist.

It has been said that the Giant possesses the intellect and mental ability of an eight-year-old child, later revealed to have actually been one. Consequently, he displays immaturity, moodiness, and high expectations, illustrated by his outburst as he devastates a city while insisting he be the President of America and an astronaut, as well as when he tearfully calls Invincible “mean” for beating him in a fight.

The Giant was originally an ordinary eight-year-old, human child living with his parents until, through some unknown means, he transformed into a gargantuan cyclops.

Gogglesvincible is an evil variant of the main Invincible and a supporting antagonist in the third season of the series. Much like most other alternate versions of Invincible, he, in one way or another, became a supervillain.

Gogglesvincible was one of the evil variants of Invincible who would be assembled by Angstrom Levy to start the Invincible War in the mainstream universe.

This Invincible's costume looks like the signature blue & yellow costume but with various noticeable changes. His shade of yellow is lighter and uses a bit darker shade of blue instead of the cyan color the main suit has. He was two black markings on each side of his body that go from his bicep to the armpit and all the way down to his thigh. His gloves are longer and go up to his elbows, making a pointed shape at the ends. Other small features are the black ends of his feet and his exposed forehead. Finally, his most prominent feature is his much bigger goggles with an additional nose bridge.

entities.name: Gravitator
entities.description:
Chris, also known as Gravitator, is a minor character in Invincible, debuting in Season 5. He is the fiancée of Hanna.

Chris is an ordinary human male of average height and build with short brown hair and brown eyes. Lacking natural superhuman physical mutations, his appearance is defined by the high-tech, mechanical gravity-distorting exo-suit and custom gravity gun he constructed out of stolen factory components. He looks like a standard scientist or technician rather than a traditional comic book villain, relying entirely on his wearable technology to manipulate gravitational fields.

Chris dons a bulky, mechanical makeshift exo-suit. Constructed entirely from stolen industrial spare parts and factory components, the heavy-duty harness has a raw, blue-collar aesthetic featuring exposed wiring and metallic plating rather than a sleek supervillain design. His look is defined by this wearable technology, specifically the custom-engineered gravity gun wired directly into his gauntlets that serves as his primary weapon for projecting concentrated bursts of localized anti-gravity energy.

The Great Wall is Mister Liu's personal bodyguard and most loyal henchman.

The Great Wall has a towering, muscular appearance. His appearance is his large and imposing physique, which shows his role as a formidable enforcer. He is typically seen wearing a light tan, utilitarian outfit that conveys his serious and silent nature. His overall presence conveys strength and unwavering loyalty to Mister Liu.

Great Wall's background is mostly unknown.

At night, Liu and Great Wall approached Titan and watched as Liu turned into a dragon to overthrow Titan.

entities.name: Green Ghost II
entities.description:
Aquarus † Darkwing † Martian Man † Red Rush † War Woman †

Alana, also known as Green Ghost, was a superheroine whose had the ability to change her density. Her origin of her powers were from an unknown green rock that would change her form into an intangible, green entity. She replaced the original Green Ghost and was a member of the Guardians of the Globe, until they were all betrayed and killed by Omni-Man.

Alana's human form was an African-American woman with chin-length dreadlocks and brown eyes. She also wore a blue top, solid pink trousers with light pink sneakers, and yellow glasses. While in her superhero form, she retains her figure albeit being entirely green and bare feet. Like all the other Guardians, Green Ghost wore a piece of equipment resembling a wristband that would signal an alert anytime her or any of the other Guardians were needed in action, however it was only worn outside of her superhero form.

Green Ghost was selfless, caring and heroic much like the other Guardians, as shown when she saves the children during the explosion over the White House by renders them intangible, and safety removed them out of the rubble . She is also quick to act in the face of danger, demonstrating bravery and selflessness, especially when protecting others, as shown when she saves bystanders from collapsing building, and later helps Red Rush evacuates citizens. Additionally, she approaches her duties with a calm and collected demeanor, often serving as a stabilizing force in the group. Green Ghost would often have fights with her husband, Theo, about their relationship, and if it should've been public or not, despite this they seemingly still cared for each other, with her death deeply affecting him. Green Ghost also showed empathy towards her allies, being in shock after seeing what Omni-Man had done to Red Rush, and even turning tangible to grab Darkwing's corpse after it got thrown in her direction, which distracts her long enough for Omni-Man to swiftly thrust his hand through Green Ghost's head, and kill her instantly.

entities.name: Hail Mary
entities.description:
Hail Mary is a gigantic kaiju creature that exists alongside many others from the second age of existence. She once fought Omni-Man and after her defeat, she was captured and enhanced by Cecil Stedman and the GDA to fight Omni-Man once more after his true motives had been revealed.

Hail Mary is an enormous kaiju, standing at least 80 feet tall, possibly even taller. She is posed on all fours, with a powerfully built, muscular body. Her head is covered in bright yellow, tentacle-like appendages that hide her mouth and any visible eyes. A terrifying mouth lurks beneath the tentacles, filled with huge, rectangular teeth in the front and a row of smaller, razor-sharp teeth behind. Hail Mary's skin is mostly dark green, with a lighter green on her underside. Sharp, white spikes stick out from her back and shoulders.

Hail Mary is one of many massive, kaiju like creatures from the second age of existence on Earth, a time that came after the first age which was filled with even more terrifying beasts. As the world moved through its different ages, she was one of the few from her age that managed to survive, eventually making it all the way to the sixth age, when humanity had taken over.

Like others of her kind, Hail Mary would rise to the surface and go on destructive rampages. Most humans, along with other beings of the sixth age, had no real understanding of where creatures like her came from or how far back their origins actually went.

entities.name: The Immortal
entities.description:
The Immortal is a supporting character in Invincible. He is an immortal superhero who has lived for thousands of years and left a significant mark on human history, assuming numerous identities throughout his life. Among these, he lived as a medieval knight, possibly associated with Arthurian legend, and later as Abraham Lincoln, before eventually adopting the superhero identity of the Immortal in the early 20th century, becoming the world's first official superhero.

He was a member of the original Guardians of the Globe and the only member to eventually return after the team was murdered by Omni-Man. Following his resurrection, the Immortal joined the newly formed Guardians and later assumed leadership of the team, replacing Robot. During this period, he also entered a relationship with Dupli-Kate, who, out of all his previous lovers, understood his struggle with experiencing death recurrently.

Following Kate's apparent death by the Komodo Dragon and his own struggles as a leader, the Immortal temporarily stepped away from the Guardians while grieving her loss. After discovering that Kate had survived, the two reunited and eventually became engaged. He subsequently returned to active duty and continued serving with the Guardians through the events of the Invincible War. In the aftermath, the Immortal retired alongside Kate, leaving superhero work behind so that the two could start a family together.

The Immortal is a tall, fair skinned man with jet-black hair, blue eyes, and a full beard with a clean-shaven upper lip. He has strong, angular facial features and a large, well-defined muscular build.

Isotope is a minor antagonist in Invincible, debuting from Season 1 and onwards. He was Machine Head's top lieutenant before becoming Titan's right-hand man.

Isotope is a Caucasian male with green hair tied back and a goatee. He wears a black shirt with a white "I" logo representing his name along with a violet business suit.

Isotope has shown loyalty to those who gain his respect, which is why he aligned with Titan instead of his previous employer, Machine Head, assisting the former in seizing control of Machine Head's criminal empire. Although he lacked formal education, he understood how to navigate the criminal underworld and consistently did his utmost to survive, particularly when confronted by The Order.

Jack Duvall is a minor character in Invincible, debuting in Season 3. He is the late son of Scott and the late Becky Duvall.

Jack was a young toddler bearing a strong resemblance to his father, having short blonde hair and many of his facial features. From his mother's side, he appeared to have her eyes.

Typical for an toddler male, Jack wore a light blue onesie.

entities.name: Jane
entities.description:
Jane is a last minute character that appears in Season 2. She is a worshiper of an ancient spirit known as Ka-Hor.

Together with her friend Riley, the two unearthed the tomb of Ka-Hor. There, Jane and Riley found the deceased father of the former who had also tried to revive Ka-Hor sometime ago and had been inadvertently trapped inside by Invincible. The two then encountered Ka-Hor himself who exuded a menacing presence before revealing his desire to possess a male host in order to escape his tomb, as well as his prejudice and disinterest in females. They were all then inadvertently sealed inside the tomb by Invincible again.

Several months later and during the Invincible War, a fight between the Immortal and an evil Invincible variant unearthed the tomb, allowing Riley to escape with a weakened Jane; the former only survived in peak condition thanks to her own abilities, and she quickly left to desert carrying Jane to get her aid.

Jane has straight blonde hair, often styled in a simple, natural way. She has a light to medium skin tone. Jane wears a casual but practical outfit for their journey to Ka-Hor, consisting of a jacket or coat over a simple top, along with pants or leggings, Jane has a beetle tattoo on her arm under her wrist.

He was seen grabbing a snack from a vending machine because he missed lunch during a shift. His superior found him, initially thinking he was an enemy, before they were both soon killed by Iguana. Jerry's throat was sliced open by Iguana's talons.

entities.name: Ka-Hor
entities.description:
Ka-Hor is a minor antagonist in Invincible, debuting in Season 1. He is an ancient undead Egyptian who was cursed and imprisoned by his own people within his tomb. Only by possessing a host and taking control of their body would Ka-Hor be able to escape his imprisonment.

Throughout the first three seasons of the series, Ka-Hor made several attempts to escape his tomb, only to fail every time thanks to some inadvertent circumstance. In most cases, this was due to his tomb being repeatedly sealed off before he could leave, or because of his initial refusal to possess a female host. His attempts at escape were also aided by cult-like worshipers who sought to revive Ka-Hor.

Eventually, after his latest attempt to possess Invincible had once again inadvertently failed, Ka-Hor grew tired of waiting and opted to possess one woman named Riley, despite her being female. Taking control of her body, Ka-Hor was finally able to escape his imprisonment.

Ka-Hor takes the form of a cursed and undead mummy. He has the dried and emaciated body while being wrapped in glowing green bandages that extend outward and act like tendrils. His eyes glow red from within a sunken face.

Kevin along with Rose and other families who live in the block owned by Machine Head, are innocent victims of Machine Head plans to burn their apartment for insurance money.

Kevin asks Titan if they ever did something to him. Rose stands behind Kevin asking him to leave Titan alone. He starts to sweat when Titan approaches him, Rose and the other families and tells them that there's a place on Third and Parklake, saying that they will put them up for a few weeks and offer them some cash money.

Kid Thor is a minor superhero character in Invincible, making his debut from Season 3 and appearing in subsequent episodes.

Wielding a massive, Enchanted-hammer, Kid Thor uses his enhanced strength and combat skills to fight alongside other heroes in the ongoing battle against supervillains.

Kid Thor is tall, broad-shouldered, and powerfully built, with the physique of a classic warrior. He has short, neatly styled blonde hair, a fair complexion, light blue eyes, and noble facial features.

His superhero outfit consists of a maroon military-style jacket with gold buttons and a high collar, beige pants tucked into maroon boots, and a simple square gold belt buckle. He wields a large hammer as his primary weapon.

Killcannon is a minor antagonist in Invincible, debuting from Season 1 and onwards.

He is a supervillain with a durable battlesuit and a laser cannon arm. He was the first villain to be defeated by Invincible and Atom Eve.

He appears to be a large, fair-skinned, muscular man. His left arm is robotic, as he wields a built in laser cannon in place of it.

His right arm lacks armor aside from a silver plate around his wrist which connects to his glove as well as as a shoulder pad. The rest of his body seems to be covered in a black suit with red markings that go under his armor. His torso is covered in a dark gray piece of armor, connecting to his robotic arm and the armor on his right shoulder. His legs, from his feet to his knees, are also covered in armor, except it is light gray.

entities.name: King Lizard
entities.description:
King Lizard, formerly known as Prince Lizard, was a supervillain and the leader of the Lizard League. He was also Queen Lizard's son.

As a child, King Lizard has green skin and a lean, athletic build. His hair is pale blonde and was formerly cut to a short, straight style

As an Adult, King Lizard’s appearance is roughly the same though more lean, taller and muscular build. His hair is also still pale blonde but more longer, roughly shoulder-length, and straight.

As a Prince, he formerly wore a two-toned green outfit with a black chest piece that featured a white lizard emblem with puffed sleeves, layered armour-like panels, and darker green gloves and boots. Around his shoulders, he also wore a magenta cape that attached beneath a high collar. On his head, he wore a gold crown shaped like a lizard’s head with eye details on the front. He also wore a dark green mask on his eyes.

entities.name: Knockout
entities.description:
Knockout is a minor character in Invincible, debuting from Season 3 and onwards.

At some point during the Great Depression, a super-villian wielded enchanted boxing gloves, providing the user great strength and durability, being able to make a regular person be able to go toe-to-toe with superhumans. At some point this villain was murdered by [https://comic-invincible.fandom.com/wiki/Thor_Man Thor Man] after getting into an altercation during a bank robbery, in which a glove fell off during. Thor Man was unknowing of his human durability without them, landing a killing blow, being shocked at his death afterwards.

Amidst the chaos, a bank security guard stole them and planned on selling them. Decades later, the guard’s grand daughter found the gloves secreted away in his home. She asked about their history. The guard told her of the gloves checkered past and when she asked for them, he happily passed them on to her. The young woman, now calling herself Knockout, became a super-heroine and began to fight crime. She quickly came to the attention of Capes Incorporated, an organization of professional super-heroes, and joined their ranks.

entities.name: Knuckle Buster
entities.description:
Knuckle Buster is one of the minor antagonists in Invincible. She, along with her husband Force Fist, were an extremist group planning to cause mass-murder and subsequently change society. The both of them were enemies of Cecil Stedman.

Knuckle Buster was a tall and curvaceous light skinned woman with long blonde hair reaching down to her lower back, thick eyebrows, and large lips. While operating as an extremist she wore a dark blue leotard which exposed her legs, with elbow length sleeves and white fur trim around her V-line which reached down to her waist. She also wore a red mask that covered her scalp, with an opening for her hair, a pair of fingerless red gloves and matching red sneaker shoes. Finishing up her costume were black knee pads, a black strap around her right hip and a red sash with the emblem of The Order of the Freeing Fist, a winged skull, as a belt-buckle.

While operating as a store clerk she dressed in an orange Indian dress, dark red pants underneath, a red cloth going around her left shoulder and right hip, a red head cloth and a pair of light-colored sneakers.

Knuckle Buster was a fanatical humanist extremist who opposed industrial life. This is shown in her overemphasis on human strength and spirit instead of using weapons such as firearms. Both her and her husband proved to be delusional, believing that through mass murder and chaos humanity would relinquish modern society for a more optimal way of life. To that end, her and Force Fist attempted to release a flesh killing bioweapon upon a city, in hopes that others would learn from their example. As the gas began to peel away at their skin, Knuckle Buster and Force Fist did not seem to mind the pain, but rather accepted it, highlighting their resolve.

Like others of his kind, Kregg dons the standard grey and white Viltrumite attire.

entities.description:
Louise was a civilian who lived in an apartment in Chicago before it was destroyed.

Louise has medium brown skin and long dark brown hair styled into a side ponytail secured with a yellow hairband. She wears triangular yellow earrings. Her outfit consists of a peach-colored top layered under a lavender-pink cardigan. Along with that she wears black pants and shoes.

Louise and her daughter were one of the survivor's of the Destruction of Chicago which destroyed their apartment building, forcing the two to live in a school gymnasium for a long amount of time.

In Chicago, Louise and her daughter watched Atom Eve rebuild a small portion of their apartment, and defended Eve when she was getting berated by a construction worker for not following the code. Louise pointed out a dilapidated area that she had been trying to get the city to clean up for over six years. Atom Eve used her powers transform the area and build a community park with a playground which the two played in.

Lucan is a supporting antagonist in Invincible, debuting from Season 2 and onwards.

He is a ruthless Viltrumite warrior of the Viltrum Empire, committed to its mission of universal domination. Following Viltrum's destruction, Lucan resettled into Earth's human society to find suitable mates to interbreed with and repopulate the Empire.

Lucan is a tall, dark-skinned Viltrumite with a bald head and the species’ signature mustache. His build resembles that of a seasoned strongman, broad and powerful, with a prominent abdomen and less defined musculature. While not sculpted like other Viltrumites, Lucan’s physique still conveys intimidating strength and brute endurance.

In his early years as a soldier of the Viltrum Empire, Lucan wore the traditional white Viltrumite uniform, symbolizing his loyalty to the empire and its brutal code of conquest.

Machine Head is a supporting antagonist in Invincible, debuting from Season 1 and onwards.

An infamous crime lord and part of an underground syndicate called the Order, Machine Head dominated Chicago's criminal underworld by instilling fear and intimidation. Nonetheless, he would quickly be usurped by his own henchman. Machine Head spent over a year in prison but would eventually reclaim authority after killing his criminal adversary and superior, Mister Liu, thereby becoming the new head of the Order.

Following the resurrection of Mister Liu and the departure of Titan, Machine Head devised an intricate plan to pit the two against each other before they were ultimately forced to rejoin the Order and under his control.

Magmaniac is a minor antagonist in Invincible, debuting from Season 1 and onwards. He is Tether Tyrant's boyfriend.

He is a supervillain who worked as a bodyguard for Machine Head. However, his criminal activities are driven by financial desperation, not a lust for power, a point emphasized in his and Tether Tyrant's attempts to find legitimate employment.

Magmaniac has a lean and athletic build, with long arms and legs that give him a tall and slightly stretched look. His body is toned in a straightforward way, not overly muscular, but clearly strong enough to handle physical conflict.

When using his powers, Magmaniac has a fiery, lava-like body, often with visible cracks and intense heat generation. In this form, his body becomes molten and he can change body structure at will.

After Mister Liu's recovery, he hired Magnattack to assassinate Titan and his family. When they were having a fun day at the park, Magnattack attacked Titan's guards and killed them all, then tried to kill Titan himself. Titan covered his body with rock, making Magnattack's attack useless against him which caused assassin to lose all of his cover. When Titan knocked him down and started beating him, Magnattack knew that he already lost, so he tried to at least kill Vanessa and Fiona. entities.name: Man Kong
entities.description:
Man Kong is a superhero who participated in the tryouts for the new Guardians of the Globe.

Man Kong has the massive, muscular build of a gorilla, though noticeably larger than a typical one. His body is covered in dark fur, except for his stomach and face, which are distinctly human-like in appearance and pale in color, while his large, powerful hands are fur-less and grey in color, resembling that of a silverback gorilla. He wears a pair of blue shorts and red sneakers, adding a touch of personality and flair to his otherwise beastly form.

Man Kong comes off as brash and overly confident, especially during the Guardians of the Globe tryouts. He seems to rely on brute strength and intimidation rather than strategy, underestimating more agile opponents like Shrinking Rae. His frustration during their fight shows he’s not used to being outsmarted, suggesting he is more of a brawler than a tactician. Despite his physical power, his quick defeat and exclusion from the team may hint at a lack of discipline or humility. There is a comedic side to him as well, whether intentional or not, as his exaggerated reactions and final face plant in his own vomit give him a slightly ridiculous, almost tragicomic vibe.

Little is known about his past, but he possesses the extraordinary ability to transform into a powerful gorilla.

The Martian Emperor is one of the minor characters in Invincible. He is the current ruler of Mars.

His backstory is largely unknown, except becoming the current emperor of all Martians.

At some point during or before the Martian Emperor's reign, a spaceship carrying a race of parasitic creatures called Sequids crashed on Mars. With their original hosts killed in the crash, the Sequid hive mind became disorganized. They attempted to possess the Martians, but the latter's shape-changing abilities enabled them to resist the Sequids. The Martians would then use the Sequids as servants, but remained cautious if they were ever to possess a non-Martian.

Martian Man was a Martian exiled on Earth and an original member of the Guardians of the Globe. He died alongside most of his colleagues when the Guardians were betrayed by Omni-Man.

Long before his arrival on Earth, Martian Man was exiled from Mars by his own race, the exact circumstances of which are entirely unknown. Taking refuge on Earth, he used shapeshifting to assume the identity of a normal human and lived in hiding until he decided to reveal his existence to the world, leading the GDA to induct him into the Guardians of the Globe. Wishing to explore his latent humanity further, Martian Man also befriended and cared for a young girl, Nikki.

Martian Man and the other Guardians of the Globe, arrive at the White House to protect the U.S. President from a sudden attack by the Mauler Twins.

Marvin is a Unopan scientist and the creator of Allen.

Marvin has a large, elongated head with deep wrinkles and ridges, giving him an aged and wise look. He has a single eye, positioned in the middle of the front of his face. He has no visible nose, with a prominent brow and a wide mouth. He is thin and frail compared to Allen, showing his non-combative nature. His design emphasizes his role as a scientist rather than a fighter.

Marvin is a patriot to his people, as he has dedicated the remainder of his years in defeating the Viltrumites and to ensure his people's survival.

Marvin was born on Unopa. Later, their home planet was attacked by Viltrumites, who were among the strongest species in the galaxies leading the Unopans to virtually go extinct. Some Unopans, including , managed to escape and abandoned their home planet.

entities.name: Matt
entities.description:
Matt is a troubled youth and the stepson of Steve.

Matt used to steal and do drugs before Steve married Molly. He lived with his dad when Steve and Molly first got together. Matt used to run wild, and be a real asshole. But he stared down his demons, and he conquered them. Steve and Molly are very proud of the man he is becoming. Since Matt is obsessed with The Beatles and wanted to go visit Abbey Road and Apple Records in his Spring Break, Steve and Molly saved some money for a trip to London to show him how much they appreciate all his hard work.

In "Here Goes Nothing", Matt and Steve visit the Buckingham Palace. Taking pictures of the palace, Matt says that its an impressive palace and ask who needs that many rooms. Steve tells him that it's not about room, it's about power and that the building has one purpose, to say: "I'm the Queen, and you are my subjects". Steve mentions that The Queen might look like an nice old lady, but she comes from a long line of tyrants who all thought they were better than the rest of us. Matt looks at the sky and saves Steve calling him dad, from the Burger Mart trash bag that Invincible had launched into the atmosphere days ago. Covered in ketchup, Matt says that he didn't know they had Burger Marts in the UK. Slowly breathing, Steve says to Matt "You called me Dad", shedding tears. They both hug.

In "You Look Kinda Dead", him and a friend of his dig up The Immortal's grave. He is worried that his stepdad could lose his job at The White House for this. His friend tells him to stop being a wuss and that they are doing something epic. He is asked if he has the schnapps. His friend’s plan was to dig The Immortal's grave to drink from his skull and get his powers. Matt tells him it's just a rumor, which his friend reply that he saw it on "[https://www.reddit.com/ Reddit]". The Mauler Twins arrive at the gravesite and reply to them to not believe everything they read on the Internet.

entities.name: Maya
entities.description:
When the Flaxans invaded the city, they killed several people. Invincible manages to get Maya out of the way when she is targeted by one of the aliens, but not in time, as she is shot in his arms. He is shot at once again, but is saved by Atom Eve who sets up a force field and defends him. Eve tells Invincible to take Maya to a hospital, since she and the rest of the Teen Team had the Flaxans covered.

Invincible storms into a hospital, but is told to freeze by GDA agents. Paramedics receive her and the agents say Invincible was cleared.

After visiting his unconscious father, Mark walks into the room of Maya, the woman he had saved. The doctor tells him that her name and that her family now knew about her injuries. Mark asks if she would be okay and the doctor says that it was too soon to tell.

After going to the hospital and finding his father was awake now, Mark went to Maya's room, but found out she had died, which Nolan described as part of the job.

entities.name: Mister Liu
entities.description:
Mister Liu is a recurring minor antagonist in Invincible, debuting in the first season and appearing throughout the series. He was the ruthless former leader of the international criminal organization known as the Order. Possessing the ability to project his soul in the form of a powerful Eastern dragon, he has proven to be a formidable opponent to crime lords such as Titan and Machine Head, as well as heroes such as Invincible.

During his confrontation with Invincible and Titan, Liu was seemingly killed by Machine Head, one of his own subordinates who sought to take control of the Order. Machine Head worked with Titan to orchestrate his downfall and subsequently seized leadership of the Order from him. Liu's bodyguard, Great Wall, later recovered his body and resurrected him, although the process left Liu severely weakened.

Following his revival, Liu had lost control of the Order and sought revenge against Titan for his role in this. He threatened Titan's family by hiring Magnattack to assassinate them. After Magnattack failed, Titan enlisted the aid of Oliver and confronted Lie while he was still weakened. Although he initially overpowered them, Invincible arrived and helped Oliver overwhelm Liu, forcing him to retreat alongside his bodyguard.

Ultimately, both Liu and Titan returned to the Order, only to discover that Machine Head, who wished to have them both return to the Order under his control, had manipulated the events surrounding their conflict.

entities.name: Mokk
entities.description:
Mokk is a minor character in Invincible, debuting from Season 2 and onwards.

He is a Dornian representative member of the Coalition of Planets.

Mokk is a large, powerfully built humanoid alien with a striking resemblance to a lion. His entire physique is heavily muscled and defined, including his large hands, each tipped with faint, claw-like nails. His body is covered in a pale, whitish-tan fur, which is especially prominent on his head. His mane-like fur flows long at the back and sides, complemented by a well-groomed, elongated beard on his chin. His eyes are distinct, featuring yellow irises set against black sclera and pupils, giving him a fierce and imposing presence.

Mokk wears layered, regal attire befitting his high rank within the Coalition. Draped over his shoulders is a tan cape that matches his kilt, both adding a sense of authority and tradition to his appearance. Beneath these, he wears form-fitting clothing in a striking combination of blue, black, and gold. His armor includes blue guards protecting his knees and lower legs, as well as gold-plated accents around his waist in the form of a detailed belt. Additional gold armor pieces adorn his wrists and shoulders, further emphasizing his status and readiness for battle.

entities.name: Narrator
entities.description:
He is often used as a narrative device to transition away from explicit content, such as sex scenes, while also shifting the focus between Earth and deep space.

In "This Missive, This Machination!", as Mark begins to have sex with Amber for the first time, the narrator appears and explains that Invincible should be given some time alone. Thus, the narrator takes the audience on a brief vignette, explaining the history of the Unopans, their conflict with the Viltrumites, and the origin story of Allen the Alien.

In "You Were My Hero", he returns to recap the events leading to Allen's incarceration and how he spent several months bonding with his fellow prisoner, Nolan, Mark's father, who was imprisoned by his people for treason. The narrator would details leading up to the moment that Allen finally commences with the break out and rescue mission to save Nolan from his execution.

entities.name: Nolan's father
entities.description:
Nolan's Father was a minor character in Invincible, debuting in Season 4's flashbacks. He was the mate of an unnamed female, and the late father of Nolan.

He was Nolan's father who, together with his mate, arranged a test battle for their son in honor of his official coming of age so he could prove that he was strong enough to be ready for his adult life, to become an officer or an agent of the Viltrum Empire. But, unfortunately for him, he was one of the Viltrumites to be killed off by the Scourge Virus.

Nolan’s father was a well-built, brawny Viltrumite, with a physique and facial features very similar to his son’s in adulthood. He had black hair with a single streak of white at the front, blue eyes, and a thick, well-groomed horseshoe moustache. His broad shoulders, defined muscles, and commanding presence that conveys both strength and authority, embodying the physicality of a seasoned warrior in his prime.

During his early years as a soldier, he donned a white plain tradition Viltrumite uniform.

She was Nolan's mother, who, together with his father, tested him in combat on his day of adulthood to prove he was strong enough to assume his role as an adult Viltrumite and potentially serve as an officer or agent of the Viltrum Empire.

Nolan’s mother was a middle-aged Viltrumite woman with a thin build and visible facial wrinkles. She had blue eyes and brown hair, which she styled in a bushy ponytail. Following Nolan’s Adulthood Ceremony, she loses her left eye in the aftermath of the battle.

Like many, she wore the standard white and grey Viltrumite uniform.

She was a Viltrumite warrior of the Viltrum Empire, she was once the first known partner of “The Great Nolan” during his early conquests. Loyal to the Viltrumite mission of universal domination, she fought alongside Nolan on various assignments. However, during a mission on the Savage Planet, she was swiftly killed by a Rognarr, marking a brutal and sudden end to her role in the empire.

Her personality remains largely unknown. However, she was once a comrade to the Great Nolan. During a mission to the Savage Planet, she was unexpectedly killed by one of the Rognarrs before she had a chance to react.

Despite her extremely old age by human standards, she had appeared as a young woman with a fair, slightly tanned complexion. She had striking green eyes and a relatively slender build, distinguishing her from many of her fellow Viltrumites who typically exhibited more muscular and athletic physiques.

entities.name: Nuolzot
entities.description:
Reunite Mark and Nolan (succeeded)|relatives=}} Nuolzot was a critical character in Invincible, debuting in Season 2. He is a Thraxan who brought Invincible to Thraxa.

The first appearance of Nuolzot comes disguised as Seance Dog, who rings the doorbell at Mark Grayson’s dorm room. Posing as a magical canine from an alternate universe where dogs are wizards, he tries to gain Mark’s trust. However, after Mark slams him to the ground during a confrontation in the forest, Nuolzot drops the act and reveals his true form.

He recruits Mark for a mission: to save the Thraxan people from an impending asteroid strike that threatens to wipe out their entire race. Mark agrees, and the two embark on a six-day journey through space. Upon arrival, however, the planet appears unharmed, prompting Mark to question Nuolzot’s real motives. He is soon brought before the planet’s monarch, who is shockingly revealed to be his father.

During the battle, Nuolzot was among the few Thraxans who survived the Viltrumites assault by taking refuge in a secure hiding place.

entities.name: Octoboss
entities.description:
Octoboss is a mutated Squidmen and supervillain. He is a minor antagonist in Season 2.

Nothing is known about Octoboss' history, all that is known is that unlike other members of his species, Octoboss was born with pink skin and grew to surpass the average size for Squidmen. Prior to the events of the show, he would take on a life of crime and become known as the supervillain "Octoboss".

Octoboss is seen with other Squidmen, hijacking a facility for highly radioactive resources, where he is greeted by Rex Splode. The two fight it out, with Octoboss gaining the upper hand due to his strength and Rex having recently recovered from an injury. Unfortunately for him, Invincible would come in to help Rex. Octoboss would eventually get defeated by Rex by his new arm implant.

Octoboss, much like other members of his species, appears as a humanoid male octopus with red eyes, no hair, and tentacles sprouting from his arms. Unlike other Squidmen, his size far surpasses the average size of his species, along with his coloring being pink rather the regular dark cyan his species are. He also possesses metal leggings to theoretically get around easier, as well as an arm cannon to deal stronger damage.

entities.description:
Omnipotus is a minor antagonist in Invincible, debuting from Season 2 to 5.

Though his origins and full abilities remain mysterious, Omnipotus serves as a dangerous threat both to the Guardians of the Globe and to Invincible himself.

Omnipotus is an alien warlord with a terrifying and monstrous presence. Towering at well over 12 feet tall, far above average humanoids, his massive frame is both bulky and powerfully muscular. His exposed skull-like face resembles that of a decayed or undead creature, featuring sharp, jagged green teeth and hollow eye sockets. A dark, spiked helmet with jagged points crowns his head, amplifying his menacing visage. His jaw appears mechanical or bone-like, adding to his eerie aura.

His pale purple skin contrasts with the dark purple armor plating that covers his torso and legs. The armor is angular and adorned with spikes and intricate, tech-inspired designs. His broad shoulders and forearms are armored and spiked, reinforcing his threatening look.

The Payton Warden, is a minor character in Invincible, debuting in Season 3. She is the warden of Payton Penitentiary.

The Payton Warden has an average height and a balanced build with a medium brown complexion. Her hair is dark with a gray stripe and is pulled back into a neat low style. Her eyes are dark brown in color and her lips are red.

She is dressed in a dark suit jacket paired with matching dark suit pants and shoes of the same color that create a consistent and professional look. Under the jacket, she wears a white blouse.

While her personality isn't deeply explored due to her minor status, her position as a warden suggests a stern, no-nonsense demeanor necessary to manage a penitentiary for super-criminals.

entities.name: Pete
entities.description:
Pete is a guard who works in the Global Defense Agency Prison.

Pete is a fair skinned male with blond hair, green eyes, and wears a prison guard uniform. After getting injured by the Maulers during their first escape, he briefly wears a cast.

On chicken pot pie night at the prison, Pete was handing out pies to various prisoners until he arrived at one of the Mauler Twins cells. Just as he was placing the pie into the food pass compartment, Robot who was watching from cameras, hacked the cell and opened the other side of the compartment. This allowed the Mauler to grab Pete by his arm and slam him against the cell, knocking him out and breaking his arm. The Mauler then proceeded to use Pete's broken arm to open his cell and the cell of his Twin.

In the aftermath of Invincible and Omni-Man battle, the Mauler Twins were recaptured by the GDA and sent back to prison. Pete was present with his arm in a cast as one of the Mauler Twins was moved back into his cell. One of them gave him a smirk as Pete walks away with an upset look on his face.

entities.description:
Polly is the name of Samantha Eve Wilkins's biological mother who was a test subject for Dr. Elias Brandyworth. She appears in the prequel story of Atom Eve.

Polly had died during the birth of Samantha forcing Dr. Elias to perform a crude C-section to deliver Samantha alive. In order to prevent the infant from being found, he swapped Samantha with the Wilkins family's stillborn daughter.

Polly's hair is Light brown, shoulder-length hair, slightly wavy. She wears a loose, maternity-friendly outfit, likely a sweater and comfortable pants, fitting her pregnant state.

After her death, Steven Erikson and his team of scientists retrieved her corpse and transformed her into a zombie-like cyborg to continue his vile experiments. In this state, Polly is extremely frail, is completely bald and is fitted with various cybernetics to ensure her body continues to function whilst being in a vegetative state due to Polly being brain dead.

Prisonincible is a supporting antagonist in the third season of the series. He is an evil variant of the main Invincible from a another universe, where he was imprisoned and brutally tortured in a Viltrumite Prison.

Prisonincible was assembled by Angstrom Levy to help start the Invincible War in the mainstream dimension. After the war, he and the surviving variants turned on Angstrom for breaking their deal and were subsequently banished to the Wasteland Universe.

Prisonincible has a physique nearly identical to his original counterpart. He is tall, but completely bald, with no hair at all. Prof. Ock is a supervillain from another universe Mark was transported to in his battle with Angstrom Levy. He is one of Agent Spider's nemesises.

Little is known about Prof. Ock's story. It is known that he is a professor or doctor of some kind, and that at one point he has built himself a giant metal "helmet" with tentacle-like arms to aid in his villainy. He's implied to be one of Agent Spider's nemeses.

During one of his battles with Agent Spider in an alleyway, a portal opened up, causing Invincible, a superhero from another dimension to enter his world and crash against him. Because of his old age and frail appearance, however, Invincible thought that Agent Spider was the villain terrorizing an old man, giving him time to attack him from behind.

It's implied that Agent Spider and Invincible had teamed-up and defeated Prof. Ock shortly after.

entities.name: Queen Lizard
entities.description:
Queen Lizard was the former leader of the Lizard League and King Lizard's mother. She would supposedly be killed due to unknown circumstances, with her son inheriting her position after her death.

Queen Lizard's body has green skin with a smooth and even tone. Her build is athletic, with clear muscle definition in her arms, shoulders, and legs. She stands upright with a firm posture. Queen Lizard's face is uncovered except for the mask she wears which possesses a golden headpiece shaped in the form of a frilled lizard. Her eyes have purple sclera with slit purple and she possesses fangs, further emphasizing her lizard theme. Her hair is pale blonde with a tint of green and styled back away from her face.

Queen Lizard wears an outfit that befits her status as royalty and her reptilian theme. The main suit is a combination of shades of green and purple. The upper section forms solid armor-like plates over her chest, while the midsection is darker and more fitted. She wears a long purple cape that hangs behind her and reaches down to her legs. Attached to the cape is a wide collar that opens outward around her neck and shoulders. The inside of the collar is purple, with its edges lined in green. Her legs are left exposed, and her waist is held by a belt with a stylized lizard emblem at the center. Below that, she wears a pair of stylized boots.

As leader of the Lizard League, Queen Lizard was shown to be fanatically devoted to her cause, declaring that in time, the world would burn and its flames would "warm the cold blood" of her and her followers as they conquered what was left. She was also a devoted mother to her son Prince Lizard, and a shrewd tactician. During the raid on the lab, she ordered the League to stay close together rather than split up and correctly inferred that the facility held valuable information when the heavy hitters of the Guardians arrived to fight the League.

entities.name: Radcliffe
entities.description:
Radcliffe is a character in Invincible, debuting in Season 3's flashbacks. He served as the director of the Global Defense Agency and was both a mentor and former superior to Cecil Stedman.

Radcliffe appears as a middle aged African-American male. He lacks any hair and possesses weathered features. After an encounter with the Lizard League, he acquired scars on the left side of his face and eye, causing it to remain shut.

His clothing consists of a gray suit with a white shirt, gray tie, and black pocket square.

Similar to his protégé Cecil Stedman, Radcliffe presents himself as a figure of calm detachment and authority, yet beneath that exterior lies a genuinely caring individual. Despite his good intentions and deep empathy, he embraces a mindset of “the ends justify the means” and “the lesser of two evils.” Driven by his dedication to the greater good, he is willing to make morally questionable decisions if he believes they are necessary to protect the planet. With a sharp eye for talent, Radcliffe refuses to let gifted individuals go to waste; instead, he believes they should be “fixed” and directed toward serving the needs of humanity.

Rex Sloan, better known as Rex Splode, is a superhero and former member of the Teen Team who later joined the Guardians of the Globe. His superhuman ability allows him to manipulate objects at the molecular level, accelerating their molecules to an unstable state of potential energy and causing them to explode.

His power is primarily channeled through special devices implanted in his forearms, allowing him to charge objects simply by touching them. He commonly carries small objects and projectiles on his person, as well as metal bars attached to his belt, giving him a ready supply of ammunition.

Although Rex initially presents himself as an arrogant and abrasive teenager, his experiences throughout his life and especially his near-death experience against the Lizard League gradually transform him into a more mature, courageous, compassionate, and heroic person.

entities.name: Riley
entities.description:
Riley is a minor character that appears in the second season. She is an ally of cult-like worshipers of an ancient spirit known as Ka-Hor who sought to revive him.

Together with her friend Jane, the two unearthed the tomb of Ka-Hor. There, Riley and Jane found the deceased father of the latter who had also tried to revive Ka-Hor sometime ago and had been inadvertently trapped inside by Invincible. Riley and Jane then encountered Ka-Hor himself who exuded a menacing presence before revealing his desire to possess a male host in order to escape his tomb, as well as his prejudice and disinterest in females. They were all then inadvertently sealed inside the tomb by Invincible again.

During the Invincible War, a fight between the Immortal and an evil Invincible variant unearthed the tomb, allowing Riley to escape with a weakened Jane; the former only survived in peak condition thanks to her own abilities, and she quickly left to desert carrying Jane to get her aid, but not before berating Ka-Hor for his sexist views after he had failed to possess the variant.

Riley eventually returned to the tomb of Ka-Hor with Invincible. However, yet another inadvertent turn of events robbed Ka-Hor of his prospective host, which led him to reluctantly possess Riley instead despite his views, and he finally managed to escape his tomb.

Rodgers is a mad scientist, partially responsible for the creation of Phase One, but primarily responsible for the development of her sibling counterparts.

Rodgers is an elderly, stern-looking scientist with a bald head and small patches of grey hair near his ears. His face shows clear signs of age, including deep lines. He has a mechanical eyepiece over his left eye with visible metallic parts and a red circular detail. His eyebrows are thick and angled.

He wears a white lab coat with a high black collar underneath.

Rodgers’s early life remains unknown. It is known, however, that he worked for the U.S. government on secret experiments aimed at creating a powerful superhuman known as Phase One, who possessed reality-bending abilities but remained under governmental control.

entities.description:
Satan, also known as The Great Beast, is a supporting character in Invincible, debuting from Season 3 to 4.

He is an ancient demon lord residing in Under Realm, who was dethroned by Volcanikka, a major threat to both the Under Realm and the surface world, and stripped of his power, leading him to seek to reclaim his former status as its supreme ruler.

Satan enlisted the aid of several demons, including Damien Darkblood, who had been banished back to Hell by Cecil Stedman and the Global Defense Agency. After failing to stop Volcanikka, Satan and Damien attempted to summon Omni-Man to Hell for assistance, but instead inadvertently summoned Invincible. Despite this, Invincible aided them, and together they helped Satan reclaim his power and throne, ultimately defeating Volcanikka.

With his crown removed, Satan appeared as a short, elderly demon with red skin, a short tail, yellow sclera with white irises, and grey hair featuring a white geometric-patterned shaved section.

entities.name: Sequid
entities.description:
The Sequids are recurring antagonist in the series making their debut in the first season.

They are a parasitic alien species known for their destructive nature and their iconic ability to control the minds of others, having left a trail of devastation across the universe before ultimately crash-landing on Mars. During their time on Mars, the Sequids were enslaved by the Martians since they required living and controllable hosts in order to become a true threat.

That situation changed when a group of astronauts arrived on Mars, with Invincible following the mission. The Sequids managed to take control of one astronaut, Rus Livingston, using him as a host to break free. They quickly unified, destroyed Mars, and then set their sights on Earth.

Their first attempt to invade Earth was stopped by the combined efforts of the Guardians of the Globe, along with Atom Eve and Invincible, who was able to save Rus. However, one Sequid secretly remained inside him and later took control again, quietly building up hosts for another invasion.

entities.description:
Lizard League Powerplex Team Evil Invincible:

Shapesmith is a supporting character in Invincible, debuting from Season 1 and onwards.

Born from the planet Mars, he is the second Martian to leave Mars and later on disguises himself as Rus Livingston in the planet Earth. He would later become a superhero and was selected as the new member of the Guardians of the Globe.

In his super hero form, Shapesmith changes his skin to appear to be wearing a blue and orange suit, with a geometric S on his chest, and appears to be wearing a blue domino mask. In his true Martian form, he doesn't appear to have any visible difference from any other Martian seen in the series, although in his brief appearance he is seen with larger orange pupils than the others.

entities.name: Shrapnel
entities.description:
Shrapnel is a minor character in Invincible.

She was a superhero and one of the many to try out for the new Guardians of the Globe roster. Eventually, she was killed in the Invincible War by Hoodvincible.

Shrapnel's body has many mechanical parts, with her left arm being fully cybernetic. Said arm has a light brown glove covering her hand but exposing her fingertips. Her right arm is identical, except with the technological part, still wearing the light brown glove. Her head has blue and white markings, with the blue surrounding her eye and the white streaking across her hair and having 4 lines on the sides of her face. Her clothing is quite basic, having a yellow vest with very light brown accents and regular pants with a belt, having two pockets along with a holster and pistol in it.

Her original whereabouts are unknown, including her powers and capabilities.

Rachel, better known as Shrinking Rae, is a major character in Invincible, debuting from Season 1 and onwards.

She is a superheroine who can reduce her size to extremely tiny sizes. After the massacre of the original Guardians of the Globe by Omni-Man, she was chosen by Robot to be part of the new version of the Guardians after successfully finishing a challenging audition process. After her close brush with death involving the Lizard League, Rachel started to reassess her life, seeking a purpose beyond being a superhero; she even found herself in a relationship with Rex Splode before his tragic end in the Invincible War.

Rae is a young woman with tan skin, green eyes, brown hair, and a well-toned, athletic physique. She also wears glasses and her hair tied back in a low, effortless ponytail.

entities.name: Slaying Mantis
entities.description:
Slaying Mantis is a supporting villain, serving from Season 3 and onward.

He wears a large, imposing battlesuit that resembles a mantis. The suit is primarily green and white, further emphasizing the insect theme. The suit incorporates sharp, angular features, mimicking the mantis's appearance.

His membership in The Order indicates a willingness to engage in criminal activities. He aligns himself with powerful villains, showing his desire for power or profit. However, he was also seen attacking civilians without much known reason, implying he may be sadistic.

Slaying Mantis is shown as one of the members of The Order during a meeting where Machine Head takes control of the organization. Machine Head goes ranting about how to change The Order or give some suggestions, and Slaying Mantis raises his hand. It is shown that Machine head calls out his name, showing that he is aware of who Slaying Mantis is then proceeds to curse him out.

entities.name: Space Racer
entities.description:
Space Racer is a supporting character in Invincible, debuting from Season 4 and onwards.

He is a legendary cosmic nomad, known throughout the universe more as a mysterious myth than a confirmed presence. A century ago, Space Racer encountered Nolan, one of the Viltrum Empire's greatest warriors, which led to his imprisonment in an asteroid. A century later, after Nolan joined the Coalition's mission, both he and Allen set out to retrieve Space Racer's weapon: the Infinity Ray, resulting in the release of Space Racer, who endured a century of inanition and was swayed to ally with the Coalition against the Viltrumites. Space Racer played a critical part in the Viltrumite War, as he tamed multiple Rognarrs and aided in Viltrum's destruction. Following the war, Space Racer remained with the Coalition.

Space Racer has a green, alien-like head with three horizontally aligned eyes, enclosed in a transparent dome helmet. He wears a form-fitting spacesuit with a bold yellow upper torso and arms, contrasted by dark brown lower torso, legs, and gloves.

His suit features utility components, a chest insignia, and two brown stripes on each upper arm. He has gloved hands, large clawed feet with an animalistic shape, and a tall, muscular build.

entities.name: Steve
entities.description:
Steve is a security guard who works at the White House and is certified in superhuman evasion training. He has a wife, Molly, and a stepson, Matt.

Steve is a middle-aged man with a somewhat rugged approachable appearance. He has short, slightly graying hair and a mustache, giving him a seasoned look. He wears a standard dark suit typical of White House security personnel.

He comes across as a kind, thoughtful, and slightly world-weary guy who cares deeply about his family, especially his stepson. In his brief scene, he talks about how his relationship with his stepson has improved, showing that he’s a patient and understanding person. He’s professional but not overly stiff, and he carries himself in a relaxed but alert manner.

He is gone for two weeks in London which is all of Matt's spring break. He doesn't have biological children, but he married a woman named Molly who had a son, Matt. Matt was a troubled youth, but ultimately overcame his problems. Matt asked to go to London, so Steve and Molly scraped enough money together to make it happen. As Steve was telling another security guard about this, the Mauler Twins arrived to try to kill the President. Steve managed to shoot out one of the Maulers' eyes, but before the Mauler Twins could kill him, the Guardians of the Globe arrived to defeat them.

Stripevincible was assembled by Angstrom Levy to help start the Invincible War in the mainstream dimension. After the war, he and the surviving variants turned on Angstrom for breaking their deal and were subsequently banished to the Wasteland Universe.

entities.name: Supreme Lizard
entities.description:
Supreme Lizard was the temporary leader of the Lizard League.

Under his command, the Lizard League begin to hit a bio research lab, they are then interrupted by Shapesmith posing as Rex Splode before the actual Rex Splode shows up with the Guardians to deal with them.

After the embarrassing defeat at the hands of the Guardians, he gives a speech for the Lizard League, trying to motivate them after being defeated. As they unenthusiastically chant "We are unstoppable!" He tells them that they are under his leadership and not King Lizard's, trying to motivate them even more. As they once again unenthusiastically chant "All Hail Supreme Lizard!", Supreme Lizard gets shot in the head by none other than King Lizard himself who came back to reclaim his position.

entities.description:
Taylor is a a one time character in Invincible, debuting in Season 2. He is a jogger, who lives in the same neighborhood as the Graysons.

One night he was jogging, possibly running for a marathon event of his own. After passing by the Grayson House, he nearly threw up but told himself that was going to succeed and feel like a million bucks. He didn't hear Invincible who arrived to the spot and made it to his house. Afterwards, he presumably continued his night jog.

entities.name: Tech Jacket
entities.description:
Zoe Thompson, better known as Tech Jacket, is a supporting character in Invincible, debuting from Season 3 and onwards.

She was one of many assets that joined the Coalition of Planets in their fight against the Viltrum Empire in the Viltrumite War.

Zoe is a fair-skinned, 15-year-old teenage girl of average height with a slim build. She has short, neck-length black hair styled in a neat bob cut, featuring straight bangs and slightly flared sides. Her bright blue eyes are accentuated with black winged eyeliner, complementing her otherwise soft facial features, which include a small, delicate nose.

Zoe wears a sleek, futuristic armored suit primarily coloured in light grey-white and dark blue, with segmented armour plating covering her helmet, chest, shoulders, forearms, shins, and feet. The suit has a streamlined, form-fitting design accented by angular panel lines and smooth contours. Her fully enclosed helmet features a rounded visor with a prominent glowing circular sensor on the forehead capable of firing lasers. Rounded shoulder pauldrons, articulated arm and leg armour, integrated gauntlets, and sturdy armoured boots finish it off.
entities.short_description: Zoe Thompson, better known as Tech Jacket, is a supporting character in Invincible, debuting from Season 3 and onwards.

entities.description:
Telia is a supporting character in Invincible, debuting from Season 2 and onwards. She is Allen's superior and girlfriend.

She is a high-ranking member of the Coalition of Planets.

Telia's build is that of a slender woman, with pinkish hair styled into five bangs. In her work attire, she wears a mostly red and sometimes black uniform, while as a civilian, she dons a small white, dark gray, and pink dress, and sometimes has tentacles.

Telia is level headed and open minded, sometimes energetic.

entities.name: Tether Tyrant
entities.description:
Tether Tyrant is a minor antagonist in Invincible, debuting from first season and onwards. He is Magmaniac's boyfriend.

He is a supervillain who worked as a bodyguard for Machine Head. However, his criminal activities are driven by financial desperation, not a lust for power, a point emphasized in his and Magmaniac's attempts to find legitimate employment.

Tether Tyrant has a solid and sturdy build, wide through the shoulders and strong in the arms. His frame is thick and muscular and his face has a squared jaw.

Tether Tyrant wears a unique sentient chestplate from which numerous tendrils can emerge. It sits over a fitted long sleeve shirt that shows the shape of his upper body. The chestplate has a large round core in the center where the tentacles emerge from. For the rest of his clothing he sturdy pants with a belt, thick black gloves on both hands, and black shoes that look ready for movement or combat. He also has a simple beanie on his head.

entities.name: Thaedus
entities.description:
Thaedus was the overarching protagonist of Invincible, debuting from Seasons 2 to 4.

As one of the most powerful figures in the Viltrum Empire, Thaedus was a high-ranking veteran warrior before he became the first Viltrumite to betray the Empire by assassinating the ruling Emperor Argall. Soon after, he founded the Coalition of Planets to oppose and contain the expansion of his own species' tyranny. Among his most significant achievements was the development of the Scourge Virus, engineered using his own DNA, which led to the near-extinction of the Viltrumite population. In the end, Thaedus was killed by Grand Regent Thragg after participating in the battle that resulted in the destruction of Viltrum. After his death, his closest ally, Allen, succeeded him as leader of the Coalition as per his wishes. Anticipating his demise, Thaedus left a final message for Allen, in which he gave clear instructions to utilize the newly upgraded version of the Scourge Virus against the remaining Viltrumite survivors, including Nolan and his two sons, Mark and Oliver Grayson.

Thaedus was extremely old, even by Viltrumite standards, and exhibited visible signs of age, including balding, white hair, and a lined face. Like all male Viltrumites, he possessed a mustache; however, to conceal his true nature, he grew a long white beard that extended to his chest. Despite his advanced age, his features remained strong and composed, showing only minor wrinkles, while he retained a highly robust physique with well-defined musculature.

During the Argall Era, Thaedus wore the traditional plain white Viltrumite uniform with the addition of a hood, highlighting his position as a member of the Viltrumite Council.
entities.short_description: Thaedus was the overarching protagonist of Invincible, debuting from Seasons 2 to 4.

entities.name: The Elephant
entities.description:
The Elephant is a supervillain who wears an Elephant costume, possessing the same strength of said animal. He is a minor antagonist in Invincible.

The Elephant wears a full-body suit that resembles an elephant. The suit is bulky and gray, mimicking the thick hide of an elephant. He has a large, stylized elephant head as a mask, complete with a trunk and tusks. His size makes him an ideal training dummy for younger heroes like Oliver. Mostly gray with possibly some metallic or armor-like textures, matching the "elephant skin" theme.

The Elephant knows he is not a top tier villain. He is a low level tough, more brawn than brains, a common brute and thug who relies on force and presence rather than schemes. He is not cruel for cruelty sake, and he is not out to inflict needless suffering. In many ways, he is a muscle for hire, though he can be quick to anger and violence.

The Elephant is a strict plant-eater and genuinely wants people to stop eating meat, but often resorts to aggressive means to achieve this despite the fact that it never works.

entities.description:
The Emperor is the emperor of all Chinese and one of the minor antagonist in Invincible, as he is the responsible for making the curse of Fung Cha's seventh grandchildrens (which results them having the ability to duplicate eachother).

The Emperor's backstory is largely unknown. As he became the emperor of China. Afterwards, the warlord helps everyone from the Emperor as he was actually evil well the warlord, Fung Cha, is the savior. One day, Fung Cha would carve a bloody path through the Emperor by killing all of his most elite guards, after his death, "he said The seventh generation after Cha's seventh grandchild would be burdened with a family too large to care for... and it would drive him mad,". Which results Fung Cha to kill him.

The Emperor died long after Fung Cha's seventh generation grandchildren was born. However, the curse actually resulted them to have the ability to duplicate themselves.

entities.description:
The Hunk is a muscular blond man who participated in the preselection for the new Guardians of the Globe as he was interested in applying. He went up against Atom Eve and loses against her in a fight. When Robot announces the new Guardians of the Globe, the Hunk is not selected as one of the members.

The Hunk was later killed by one of the Evil Invincibles in the Invincible War.

The Hunk's build is that of a very muscular body builder, he has blond straight hair, no shirt, and wears only shorts.

Very little was seen of the Hunk's personality, save for the fact that he appeared to be somewhat arrogant and egotistical because of his muscles.

entities.name: Theo
entities.description:
Theo is a minor character in Invincible, debuting on Season 2. He is the widower of Green Ghost II.

Theo is a tall man with a medium to dark complexion and a lean build. He has short dark hair and defined features that give him a composed look.

He wears a gray jacket over a white collared shirt, paired with beige pants and brown shoes.

Before his wife's murder, he was a devoted man who cherished his wife above everyone and everything. Nonetheless, following her murder, he fell into a deep depression and found it impossible to advance in his life. He loathed Omni-Man for murdering his wife and also blamed Debbie for not revealing the truth about him earlier.

entities.name: Thraxan
entities.description:
The Thraxans are a peaceful alien species native to the planet Thraxa, known for their striking resemblance to praying mantises.

The Thraxans are a vibrant cyan-blue insectoid species resembling mantises. They possess two multifaceted red eyes and a pair of antennae. Their two arms are adorned with long, sharp spines, and each hand has two fingers, while their forelegs end in two toes.

The Thraxans are a sentient insectoid species native to the planet Thraxa, and at one point in their history, they became capable of space travel.

After Nolan left Earth, deeply shaken by his confrontation with Mark and the realization of his actions, he encountered a Thraxan ship while searching for a place to end his life. Instead, he saved the ship and its crew. In gratitude, they brought him back to Thraxa, where he eventually formed a relationship with their queen, Andressa. The two later had a son together, who would be called Oliver Grayson.

Three-Eyes is a minor background character appearing in Season 3. He is best known for sharing a cell with Cecil during Cecil's time at prison.

Three-Eyes appears as a blue sumo wrestler, he has white paint on his face and a gem in the middle of his forehead. He has only been seen wearing a standard prison outfit. His body is also big, larger than a average human.

There is almost nothing known about his personality. Three-Eyes is known for sharing a cell with Cecil during Cecil’s time in prison.

entities.name: Throwbolt
entities.description:
Throwbolt is a superheroine who operates in the United States and possesses powerful electrical abilities. She is a young, athletic hero who sought membership in the Guardians of the Globe following the death of the original team. Although she demonstrated considerable combat potential during the Guardians' recruitment trials, she ultimately failed to secure a position on the team.

Throwbolt subsequently became involved in several major events, including Doc Seismic's attack, the Invincible War, and the aftermath of the war in New York City. Despite being a relatively minor superhero, her participation in these events demonstrates her willingness to fight alongside other heroes against powerful threats and her considerable resilience in battle.

Throwbolt is a young woman with a slender, altheltic build. She has spiky blonde hair in a hairstyle resembling a faux hawk, thin black eyebrows, and blue eyes. While in her electrical state, her entire body emits a yellow glow and her eyes become solid white.

Throwbolt wears a superhero outfit consisting of a primarily yellow form-fitting sleeveless tight suit with a high-neck collar and white shapes, including two distinct thunderbolts on the front of her suit. She also wears yellow gloves with a white strip at the wrists and yellow boots.

She is a relentless Viltrumite warrior of the Viltrum Empire, committed to its mission of universal domination. Following the destruction of Viltrum, Thula settled into Earth's human society to search for suitable mates to interbreed with and repopulate the Empire.

Titan is a supporting antagonist in Invincible, debuting from Season 1 and onwards. He is the husband of Vanessa and the father of Fiona.

He was a supervillain enforcer, who once worked for the crime lord, Machine Head, due to owing him debt. When Machine Head refused to let him out of his debt, he teamed up with Invincible and the Guardians of the Globe to take him down. After Machine Head was defeated, Titan took over his organization and became a crime boss in order to provide for his family and for the people of Chicago. Eventually, Chicago evolved into an improved setting for all underprivileged neighborhoods. Criminal actions continued, yet adherence to strict regulations was essential; as a result, minimal lives were lost.

When he is not using his powers, Titan appears as a muscular African-American male with above-average height. He lacks any hair and prior to becoming a crime boss, usually wore a grey hoodie, dark grey sweatpants and timberland boots . After he took over Machine Head's criminal organization, he started sporting a nicely tailored black tuxedo with a grey tie.

Tsing Cha is a minor character in Invincible, debuting in Season 3's flashbacks.

He is the father of Dupli-Kate and Multi-Paul.

As the father of Kate and Paul, he had to deal with his children who had the gift of multiplying indefinitely while trying to support them and take care of all the children, after his wife died giving birth to them, which ended up driving him insane. After going crazy, the GDA sent him to a mental hospital and took custody of his children, training them to become assassins. Kate still visited him to see if his state changed.

entities.name: Universa
entities.description:
Universa is a minor antagonist in Invincible, debuting from Season 4 and onwards.

Universa is determined, single-minded, and pragmatic, driven by the survival of her people above all else. She showed little patience for obstacles, willing to bypass or overpower anyone in her way to achieve her goals. Her methods also are aggressive and uncompromising, even when they endanger innocent humans, reflecting her focusing on the greater purpose she believes in.

Despite her ruthlessness, Universa demonstrates discipline and control over her powers, using strategy and precision rather than relying on brute force alone. She is also capable of acknowledging limits, as seen with her respect for the Staff of Leadership, that only the ‘chosen’ can wield it. Though she showed a sense of urgency and moral justification for her actions, she rarely communicated or negotiated, instead letting her power and determination dictate the outcomes.

Universa's past remains largely unknown, as she hails from a planet far beyond Earth's star system. With her homeworld facing collapse due to a catastrophic energy crisis, she concluded that the only way to save her people was to siphon energy from Earth.

entities.name: Unopan
entities.description:
The Unopans are a race of aliens that were native to the planet Unopa until its destruction by the Viltrum Empire.

The Unopans are a humanoid species, with three fingers on each hand and two large toes on their feet. Their skin is orange and heads are conical shaped and dominated by a single eye and lack any kind of nose.

At some point before the events of the series, the Viltrum Empire who, in their aim to expand their empire, attacked the Unopan's homeworld of Unopa. This led to the Viltrumites destroying the planet when the Unopan's rebelled against them.

With their planet destroyed, the Unopans were forced to create breeding camps to prevent their species' extinction.

entities.name: Val
entities.description:
Valerie, or Val for short, is a minor character in Invincible: Atom Eve. She was once the best friend of Samantha Eve Wilkins before the discovery of latter's superpowers drove them apart.

It was later revealed that she was one of the victims who would meet her demise in the Invincible War.

She typically has a casual look, often dressed in practical clothing suited for comfort rather than flair. Her hair is short and neatly styled and has a brown completion. At age 12 her hair grows longer and had a few blackheads under her eyes.

Val was a kind and supportive person. She often helped Eve through tough situations and gave her emotional support when needed. Val had a calm and easy-going demeanor, and she genuinely cared about Eve's well-being.

She initially dressed in standard, lower-class homemaker outfits.

Following her husband's ascent to power, she started to don fashionable attire to represent her status as her husband's business partner.

Vanessa is depicted as a devoted spouse and a loving mother who desires only the finest for her family. She shows annoyance at her husband's inability to exit the crime world but wholeheartedly accepts it when he takes over Machine Head's influence and joins her as a partner in the enterprise.

Vidor was a blond male Viltrumite sporting a classic Viltrumite mustache. Vidor seemed to have two screw bolts on his head. And his overall physique looks thinner and less muscular than Nolan's, but more agile.

Vidor dressed in a classic white Viltrumite uniform and had a transparent yellow visor on his eyes.

entities.name: Volcanikka
entities.description:
Volcanikka is a supporting antagonist in Invincible, debuting in Season 4.

She is a powerful lava monster from the fourth age of existence on Earth. She is the leader of the Magmanites and the Vile, known for her attempt to free the latter in order to seize control of Hell and overthrow its ruler, Satan. After taking over Hell, she intended to do the same to the surface world and wipe out humanity, allowing her to expand her empire for reasons that remain unknown.

In an effort to stop Volcanikka and thwart her plans, Satan enlisted the aid of several demons, including Damien Darkblood, who had been banished back to Hell by Cecil Stedman and the Global Defense Agency. After failing to stop her themselves, Satan and Damien attempted to summon Omni-Man to Hell for assistance. Instead, they inadvertently summoned Invincible, who agreed to help them regardless. Together, they ultimately defeated Volcanikka, who retreated but not before swearing vengeance against Invincible.

Volcanikka appears as a tall and slender female entity whose body is composed of rock and molten magma. Her face resembles a skeletal mask, with long, bright orange flames flowing behind her as if they were hair.

Not much has been provided so far in reference to Vorg's history other than he gets up to "All manner of household adventures."
