The Walking Dread is a supporting villain, serving from Season 3 and onward.

The Walking Dread is hulking and corpse-like, with green skin and rotted lips and teeth. The top half of his head is covered by a metal helmet.

As one of the Order members, The Walking Dread is very power hungry person, willing to put other people in danger in order to gain more power. He is also very arrogant, as he begged Tech Jacket to blast him with more energy what eventually lead to his defeat.

At some point, The Walking Dread joined The Order to have unimaginable amount power and money. After Machine Head took over as leader of the Order and later tricked his enemy, Titan, and former leader Mister Liu to join the Order, so they all can have protection, power and not to be afraid of any internal conflict, The Walking Dread was seen in a power plant where he absorbed electricity to make himself more powerful. However, Tech Jacket appeared and fought with The Walking Dread. In the even fight, Tech Jacket decided to use her suit energy to blast The Walking Dread away. At first, he enjoyed this, because he was getting more power, but after a moment he was overwhelmed with the power and begged young hero to stop. She didn't, and The Walking Dread ended up losing the fight.

Not much is known about War Woman's past, except that she came from a different age, possibly indicating that, like another colleague of hers, she was thousands of years old by the time of her death.

War Woman arrived at a facility under attack by the Lizard League along with Immortal, Aquarus, Black Samson and the original Green Ghost. Gary Hampton, better known as the Wolf-Man, is one of the minor characters in Invincible, debuting from Season 3 and onwards. He is a werewolf superhero.

Wolf-Man is a werewolf with grey-light skin, muscular, yellow eyes, except with the tail like other werewolves who does not have a tail in some legends.

Gary Hampton was a wealthy record company CEO who was happily married to his wife Rebecca, with whom he had a teen daughter named Chloe. But one night while camping he was attacked by a werewolf, and thus later became one himself. entities.description:
He is a low-ranking member of the Coalition of Planets.

Worg is a tall humanoid man with a very muscular built comparable to Allen's. He sports watercolor-colored skin accompanied by oil-colored hair and beard, and wears a standard Coalition uniform consisting of a full-sleeve, black collared up yellow shirt with an Emblem like Captain Pikell's. He also wears black pants with a silver metallic belt and black shoes.

Little is known about Worg personality, but he gives the impression of being a serious man who tries to address the problems that arise on the ship. This can be seen when it immediately extinguishes the fire that ignites on the Venture's control panels, and later when he votes alongside the other crew members to replace the incompetent Captain Pikell with General Telia.

He along with the rest of Captain Pikell crew welcomes Allen, Telia and Nolan into their ship. When the gang arrive on the ship they are greeted warmly by the Captain who explains how his ship has the best accommodations and hospitality throughout the entire coalition. Of course, this doesn't compliment with the condition of the ship which is rundown and is in desperate need of repairs, with even it's equipment catching fire due to short circuits.

entities.name: Zak
entities.description:
Zak is an African American, with short, curly, and dark hair, typically wears a yellow shirt with a striped blue and yellow sweatpants.

Zak has a warm, supportive, and curious personality. Zak is shown as a good friend to young Eve. He is not dismissive or competitive and values her intelligence, treating her with respect. He is genuinely interested in learning, especially when Eve explains science to him. Rather than being intimidated by her brilliance, he appreciates it.

Little is known about Zak, other than how he was a babysitter that the Wilkins hired to take care of Samantha when they went out for a date.

One night, the Wilkins went out, and Zak was asked to take care of a young Sam. Zak was assured Eve could handle herself. while he was busy prepping for an upcoming test at his school. Sam takes a look at his book and Zak asks her about electrons, to which she says something interesting about electrons, and mercury, being unusually aware and adept with chemistry at a young age. This attracts his interest and Zak asks her more questions.

entities.description:
Dinosaurs are animals from prehistoric period prior to the rise of mankind. In an alternate universe, they remain the dominant species and have virtually wiped out humans from hunting them for food.

Approximately 66 million years ago, dinosaurs ruled the Earth, until an impact event caused a mass extinction that wiped all of them out. The event paved the way for humans to evolve and eventually dominate the planet in our universe.

At some point in the Modern Era, a Doctor named David Anders, was studying the Dinosaur species and accidentally mutated himself and became Dinosaurus.

In I Thought You Were Stronger, Angstrom used his powers to send Invincible into a dimension where the dinosaurs survived and even existed among humans. However, the former desires to eat the latter, finding them to be a rare and delicious delicacy. They also exhibited intelligence and were even capable of speaking.

They are cybernetic enhanced beings that assisted Angstrom Levy in the Invincible War.

Technicians are gray-skinned, cybernetic upgraded humanoids that are more mechanical than organic, donning orange tunics with black accents.

They appear to be very detached, unfeeling people with mysterious intentions. Having a low tolerance for deception, they planned to permit Angstrom Levy to experience a drawn-out, tormenting end if he refused to submit to their servitude.

The story behind the Zombies is generally unknown. At one point in time, an unknown virus that reanimates its victims struck Earth, causing a potentially global zombie apocalypse.

Angstrom Levy had once encountered a dimension consumed by a zombie virus, later sending Invincible to it during their battle. Invincible managed to escape the zombies and find a group of survivors, whom he tells about Angstrom Levy and his current predicament before a portal to his world opens.

entities.name: Flaxan
entities.description:
The Flaxans are a race of inter-dimensional beings that were set on conquering planet Earth and killing its humans. They made several attempts to invade Earth and each time they arrived, the Flaxans were defeated by various superheroes.

Following their third invasion attempt which ended in their defeat thanks to Omni-Man, he followed the Flaxans back to their home dimension and completely destroyed it, leaving their civilization in ruins and killing numerous Flaxans, before returning back to Earth. The Flaxans were put out of commission for several years but were eventually able to recover.

They soon returned for a fourth invasion attempt, but were once again thwarted by the combined efforts of the Guardians of the Globe and Invincible. Aware that they could return stronger than before, Robot and Monster Girl along with the rest of the Guardians attempted to follow the Flaxans back to their dimension to stop them once and for all. However, only Robot and Monster Girl were able to make through before the portal closed, leaving the two stranded in the Flaxan Dimension with the Guardians unable to follow.

In the first attempt of the invasion of Earth, the Flaxans teleported into the downtown area of the city, where they began killing every human they saw. The police attempted to fight back but were easily outgunned and outnumbered by the Flaxans. Invincible spotted one of the Flaxans about to murder an old woman and threw a piece of debris at it, injuring the Flaxan. Invincible saved the old woman, but due to tripping while flying, the woman's legs were bashed and she was left in critical condition.

The Order of The Freeing Fist was a cultist group that attempted to wipe out a large quarter of humanity, but was stopped by Cecil Stedman.

It is currently unknown how the cult started and how many more members are there besides Knuckle Buster and her Husband, Force Fist. Much like Doc Seismic, the couple of the Cult at large believe that by reducing the population the world could heal from much of the damages caused to the environment.

The couple ran a spiritual store by a beach as a cover up to release Chemical X upon the entire city. Once activated in the storage unit of the store, the bomb would leak harmful chemical gasses causing anyone nearby to die instantly as their skin burns away. Cecil, when he was an agent of the GDA was tasked to lead a task force to stop the cultists before they could kill civilians.

entities.name: Team Evil Invincible
entities.description:
Team Evil Invincible are a group of major antagonists of Season 3 and onwards. They are a collection of ruthless Invincible variants from across the multiverse, assembled by Angstrom Levy from their universes as part of his plan for revenge against the mainstream Invincible.

In exchange for their services, Angstrom promised many of the variants access to alternate realities to expand their empires. Together, they launched a devastating assault on the mainstream dimension, igniting a brutal war that raged for over three days. They clashed with numerous superheroes and defenders, overwhelming many and leaving a trail of casualties, though their own ranks were reduced to less than half by the conflict’s end.

Near the end of the third day, Angstrom Levy summoned the surviving variants, only for them to attempt a sudden betrayal. In response, Angstrom banished them to a desolate Wasteland Universe. Meanwhile, the fallen variants’ bodies were collected by the G.D.A. and repurposed into ReAnimen, intended as weapons against the looming threat of the Viltrum Empire. Regardless, their actions brought terror, trauma, and widespread destruction to the people and heroes of Earth, surpassing even Omni Man's rampage in Chicago.

Each of these Invincible variants hails from a universe where, in some form, they embraced malevolence. While some allied with Omni-Man, others developed their own twisted mindsets, becoming even more dangerous in their descent into villainy. Regardless of their path, all of them brought death and destruction to their respective worlds. This was apparently something common throughout the multiverse and most variants of Invincible would become evil in one way or another.

entities.name: The Order
entities.description:
The Order is an international secret society and organized crime network overseen by a council of supervillain crime bosses. They are one of the largest, most powerful and influential criminal organizations on Earth, ruling the local underworlds of many nations.

At an unknown period of time, the Order was formed by members of the most dangerous supervillain crime bosses on Earth.

At a certain time in their past, Mister Liu took charge of the Order and led it effectively for numerous years, standing against attempts by some members, such as Machine Head, to dethrone him, including Set, a powerful figure who disappeared for unknown reasons. Upon discovering that Titan had supplanted Machine Head, he reached out to the new crime leader of Chicago and issued firm orders to liberate Multi-Paul from his imprisonment at Payton Penitentiary. Understanding that Titan would never acknowledge his role in the Order, Mister Liu schemed to eliminate him permanently, ultimately resulting in his dismissal as the head of the Order. A fled escaped Machine Head collaborated with Titan to remove Liu from his role in exchange for Machine Head seizing control of the organization, a scheme that was successful.

Upon taking charge of the Order, Machine Head fulfilled his commitment to Titan by permitting him to govern Chicago autonomously while he oversaw the Order.

entities.name: Viltrum Empire
entities.description:
The Viltrum Empire are the main antagonistic faction of Invincible.

Founded and led by the first Emperor, Argall, the Empire is comprised of Viltrumite warriors dedicated to expand its dominion across the galaxy and ultimately the entire universe.

An elite protective unit tasked with safeguarding the Emperor or the Grand Regent. Members are selected from among highly skilled Viltrumite warriors and are distinguished by their red ceremonial uniforms, often featuring hooded designs and modified insignia. Their role is ceremonial and defensive rather than administrative or command-based, and they operate directly under the authority of the Emperor. Though, this later became defunct in the aftermath of the Scourge Virus.

While Viltrumite uniforms follow a standardised design, variations in insignia are used to visually distinguish individuals of exceptional status within the Empire. Elite warriors, military commanders, and high-ranking officials may wear uniforms featuring refined variations of the traditional Viltrumite emblem, representing their authority, achievements, and recognition among the Empire’s highest ranks. These variations are distinguished by additional design elements incorporated into the original emblem.
entities.short_description: The Viltrum Empire are the main antagonistic faction of Invincible.

entities.name: Viltrumite
entities.description:
Viltrumites are a highly advanced alien race of exceptionally powerful superhumanoids native to their destroyed home planet, Viltrum. As the dominant species of the Viltrum Empire, they pursue an expansionist doctrine aimed at universal conquest and absolute dominion over other civilizations. They are feared across the known universe as a disciplined but merciless militaristic society that is driven by ideological supremacy and the belief that strength determines legitimacy.

Under the first Emperor, Argall, Viltrumite ideology was formalized into a disciplined imperial doctrine emphasizing strategic thinking alongside martial supremacy. This created a thoroughly coordinated expansionist civilization in which conquest, governance, and cultural enforcement operated as unified systems. Argall's legacy officially established the principle that only the strong may shape the future of the Empire, a doctrine that would later be intensified under Grand Regent Thragg.

thumb|left|200x200px|Through Argall's tactical wisdom, his people were guided to reach the heights of their potential. thumb|left|200x200px|Thragg|Thragg proved himself to be the epitome of Viltrumite traditions. thumb|left|200x200px|Even long after his death, the Viltrumites continue to follow Argall|Emperor Argall's wisdom. thumb|left|200x200px|Viltrumites such as Conquest can be reduced to hopelessly unstable, bloodthirsty beasts. A key feature of Viltrumite culture is an extreme form of Darwinism supported by rigid discipline and a belief in their own racial superiority. Established under Emperor Argall, their society judged individuals by strength, capability, and usefulness. Weakness was considered both a liability and a threat to the Empire, with those deemed unfit often eliminated to preserve the species' overall strength. Viltrumites emphasize measured power, tactical effectiveness, and the disciplined appeal of force rather than indiscriminate brutality, ensuring stability and imperial cohesion while reinforcing the belief that the weak are expendable.

The expansion of the Viltrum Empire is driven not only by conquest but also by the belief that Viltrumites possess a natural right to rule over lesser species. Their social hierarchy is based primarily on demonstrated strength and ability. Conquered worlds that prove useful may be integrated into the Empire and granted technological or infrastructural advancement in exchange for complete obedience. Those that continue to resist are often subjected to military suppression, large-scale devastation, or outright extermination.

entities.name: Viltrumite Auxiliaries
entities.description:
The Viltrumite Auxiliaries were an unnamed alien species that have been subjugated by the Viltrumites and forced to serve in various roles throughout the Viltrum Empire's military.

Almost nothing is known about this species, though Nolan mentions that they are enslaved by the Viltrumites. As such, they were forced to serve as slaves, prison guards, pilots, and soldiers for the Empire's military.

In the distant past after the purge, many of these grunts lived on Viltrum, some were seen transporting cargo for the warships, but when one became exhausted and dropped a crate, their neck was snapped by a supervising Viltrumite.

During the opening stages of Scourge Virus, many of these aliens were present when the Viltrumites were dying across the streets of the city. Upon being informed of the devastation being caused by the virus, Grand Regent Thragg ordered all non-Viltrumites on the planet to be killed in order to prevent information of the deteriorating state of Viltrum to spill out across the universe. As such, groups of Viltrumites hunted down these aliens throughout the streets of the city.

entities.name: Spouses of Superheroes
entities.description:
The Spouses of Superheroes, or SOS for short, is a therapy community group to help nurture widowed spouses of superheroes who were killed in their duty to help others.

The Spouses of Superheroes association was created to support the recovery of widowed partners of superheroes who died while serving. Soon after the murder of the Guardians of the Globe, Olga, Red Rush's widow, joined the group to find some sense of closure.

Debbie Grayson arrives at the group and converses with Theo, the widower of Green Ghost II. After Debbie discloses that she is the ex-wife of the Guardians' murderer, Omni-Man, Theo insists she must leave and not come back for their safety, and she never does.

entities.name: Atom Eve's siblings
entities.description:
Atom Eve's siblings, Phases 2 through 5, were man made experiments, made to be the successors of Phase 1, but were considered faulty.

After Brandyworth left the government, another scientist was ordered to make new warriors and essentially recreate Phase One. However, the scientist in question could not replicate Brandyworth's skills, resulting in half baked products. Most of them did not know how to speak and none of them could live longer than a day outside their pods, though they still possessed formidable powers. In creating them, the government would use Polly, the one they used to create Phase One and who died during childbirth. They had managed to revive her but she was left brain dead and in horrible physical condition.

Some years later, Erickson ordered the release of Phases Two through Five, upon learning of Phase One's status. They managed to lure Phase One, known as Atom Eve to a nearby downtown highway where they learned of each other relations to one another and their purposes. The Phases fought Eve, and most of them died out from the experience and due to their unstable bodies. Brandyworth claimed because he was not working for the government, the Phases did not have the same experience or capability that Eve did. Phase Two died in Eve's arms, claiming he wished things were different.

At home, Eve found disgust over her parents eating her birthday cake as punishment, and found a shattered portrait and materialized a new one of the phase 2-5 creations, Polly and Brandyworth and herself as way to remember them all.

Peter Claver Cullen (July 28, 1941 - August 26, 2026) was a Canadian Emmy Award-Winning voice actor who voices Thaedus in Invincible.

Born from their own different planets, one of their home planet was invaded by the Viltrum Empire—one of the species were imprisoned and were held captive in the asteroid prison.

In the year 2024, they were still imprisoned and alive as most of them others were executed. But now, when two executioners decides to execute Nolan for committing treason against the Viltrum Empire, Allen began to free prisoners one-by-one. After freeing the prisoners, they began to slaughter the Prison Alien Guards but all of them were killed.

The species has different abilities that can kill one of the Prison Alien Guards, excluding the Viltrumites. The species can be easily be killed and cannot be survived by the Alien Guards' weapons and the Viltrumites.

entities.name: Mayor of Chicago
entities.description:
The mayor of Chicago is the  chief executive of city government in Chicago, Illinois, the third-largest city in the United States. The mayor is responsible for the administration and management of various city departments. In addition, the Mayor submits proposals and recommendations to the Chicago City Council, is active in the enforcement of the city's ordinances, submits the city's annual budget and appoints city officers, department commissioners or directors, and members of city boards and commissions.

During sessions of the city council, the mayor serves as the presiding officer. The mayor is not allowed to vote on issues except in certain instances, most notably where the vote taken on a matter before the body results in a tie.

The office of mayor was created when Chicago became a city in 1837.

entities.name: Atlantean
entities.description:
Aquaria}} The Atlanteans are an aquatic race native to Earth who inhabit the underwater kingdom of Atlantis.

Atlanteans appear as anthropomorphic fish with humanoid bodies, fins growing from their heads, backs, arms, and legs, and webbed hands and feet. Their skin varies in colour, including tan, pink, and blue.

Atlanteans are a biologically aquatic species naturally adapted to thrive under the extreme pressures and frigid temperatures of the deep ocean. Their anatomy allows them to survive environments that would be immediately lethal to most terrestrial beings. Many Atlanteans also possess the innate ability to manipulate water through hydrokinesis, generating streams, barriers, and projectiles with precision and force.

Atlanteans possess dense musculature and durable bodies, allowing them to withstand crushing oceanic pressures and endure physical trauma beyond the capabilities of ordinary humans. Certain members of the species, including Aquarus and Aquaria, have demonstrated amphibious traits, allowing them to survive both underwater and on land through adaptations that enable normal breathing in either environment.

Capes Inc. (Capes Incorporated) is a team of superheroes comprising of many members. They are a private "Hero-for-Hire" superhero corporation that work alongside the Global Defense Agency.

Not much is known about them other than being their own superhero team outside of the Guardians of the Globe and that they met Invincible at some point.

The team were among the many heroes fighting the Invincible variants during the war. When Movincihawk attacked the Payton Penitentiary, the trio were quick to react. After Invincible took down Movincihawk, Bolt, Kid Thor and Knockout attacked the mainline Invincible, mistakening him for one of the variants. The trio attacks Invincible, without giving him a chance to talk until Movincihawk recovers and took out Powerplex, who was attempting to join the fight. Capes Inc. then teams up with Invincible to take down Movincihawk. As Atom Eve flies above the four, Invincible tells them that he needs to find out who caused this and Bolt assures him that they can handle it. After Invincible flies away with Atom Eve, Bolt instructs Knockout and Kid Thor to bring in Movincihawk who wakes up and flew away.

Cerberus is a powerful guardian creature of the Under Realm, Volcanikka banished it to the Bottomless Pit to guard Satan’s molten crown after she took over the realm.

Cerberus is a massive, three-headed beast. Each head has glowing eyes and sharp fangs, and it also has a large, powerful tail.

Originally, Cerberus served as the guardian of the entrance to the Under Realm.

During Volcanikka's rise to power, Cerberus failed to stop her from casting Satan’s molten crown into the Bottomless Pit and was subsequently banished there to serve as its guardian. Its immense strength made it nearly impossible for anyone in the Under Realm to retrieve the crown.

entities.description:
While the general "natural form" of a demon isn't fully shown, individual demons have distinct appearances. For example, Damien Darkblood has a large, imposing, red-skinned, horned, and muscular humanoid form, while the Satan is described as a short, elderly, red-skinned demon with a short tail.

Little is known about their races, but they have most likely existed since the beginning of Hell. They were once ruled by the demon known as Satan, but eons later, Satan was dethroned by unknown causes and later became the Demon Lord. Since then, he has yearned to reclaim his position on the infernal throne. At some point, a demon named Damien Darkblood managed to escape Hell for a time, exchanging his freedom to become a detective and later convincing a superhero named Martian Man on an unknown "crucial mission."

In modern days, Darkblood noticed that all the members of the Guardians of the Globe were killed by an unknown killer, Damien began investigating the murders of the Guardians, but not for long; he was banished by Cecil Stedman and the Global Defense Agency back to Hell.

In early 2024, not long after the Invincible War and Conquest's arrival, Darkblood summoned Satan and told him that he is aware of a living inhabitant who possesses immense strength, comparable to what Earth hasn't encountered for ages. He told him that he would try to summon this individual to Satan as he might aid him in returning him to his former status as the ruler of Hell.

entities.description:
The Dornians are a war-mongering, lion-like alien species.

The Dornians are typically depicted as light-furred, large feline-like creatures. Many have ponytail-like braids and are characterized by large, muscular physiques.

Since the Dornians share similar traits to that of Lions, they presumably share similar levels of sexual dimorphism, with the males sporting large manes and the female Dornian shown in Season 4 lacking a mane- much like female lions. However, unlike male lions, male Dornians are capable of growing large beards as seen with Mokk.

Although little is known about their culture, Battle Beast’s behavior suggests that the Dorinins originate from a society shaped by war and chaos.

The Gelderians are a highly intelligent humanoid species known for their scientific and technological expertise, most notably for creating the advanced armoured suit worn by Tech Jacket.

Little is known about the Gelderians as a species, aside from their exceptional intelligence and technological advancement. At some point, they became a target of the Viltrum Empire, prompting their Emperor to seek assistance from the Coalition of Planets.

Recognising that they were physically incapable of resisting the Viltrumites, the Gelderians developed a technological countermeasure known as the Tech Jacket, an advanced exo-suit designed to grant its wearer enhanced strength, durability, and combat capability.

entities.name: Human
entities.description:
Humans are the dominant intelligent species native to Earth, serving as the planet’s primary sentient life form. Within a cosmos crowded by alien civilizations, humanity is defined by its rapid technological adaptability and sheer mental resilience. Despite lacking innate cosmic supremacy, their extraordinary genetic compatibility and unyielding survival instinct allow them to produce powerful superhuman protectors. This resilience ensures they consistently punch above their weight class, remaining a pivotal player on the galactic stage.

Humans are a deeply complex species, defined by the volatile friction between their highest virtues and lowest impulses. While capable of profound empathy, moral reasoning, and cooperative progress, humanity is frequently compromised by fear, greed, and deeply entrenched systemic prejudices that fracture societies from within. The rise of super-powered individuals only intensified these dynamics, acting as a disruptive catalyst that magnified questions of control, responsibility, and existential vulnerability. This unprecedented paradigm shift effectively shattered traditional power structures, forcing an ordinary population to confront its own insignificance while balancing the terrifying thin line between superhuman heroism and catastrophic corruption.

Ultimately, humanity remains an intricate study in contradictions, forever suspended in a delicate equilibrium between hope and despair, order and chaos, light and shadow.

Humans are biologically standard primates with moderate physical capabilities, but their species is defined by remarkable cognitive flexibility and psychological resilience. Their true strength doesn’t lie in extreme force but intellect, creativity and adaptability. They are capable of developing advanced technology, complex societies, and intricate strategies to overcome challenges far beyond their physical limitations.

entities.name: Martian
entities.description:
The Martians are an alien race that live on the planet Mars, a neighbor to the planet Earth. All of them are able to use shape-changing abilities to become anything they desire. The ruler of this alien race is The Emperor of Mars.

Sometime ago, Mars was invaded by parasitic, mind-controlling aliens known as the Sequids but the Martians powers rendered them unaffected by the Sequids. With no hosts to control, the Sequids were left under the complete control of the Martians who used them as their slaves. This changed, however, when a team of astronauts went to Mars with Invincible shadowing the mission.

The Martians capture the astronauts and Invincible and bring them to the Emperor who aimed to kill the former to prevent the Sequids from unifying and rising up. Invincible and the astronauts escape but unbeknownst to any of them, a martian had replaced one of the astronauts who was then claimed by the Sequids which allowed them to invade Mars. With the enslaved astronaut, the Sequids conquered the Martians before proceeding to head towards Earth to do the same. However, the Sequids machinations were thwarted by Invincible and Guardians of the Globe, and the Martians were freed.

Martians are a highly adaptive, metamorphic species native to the subterranean cities of Mars. Their unique biology allows them to manipulate their bodies in ways that extend far beyond conventional physical limits.

entities.name: Police Enforcer Units
entities.description:
Police Enforcer Units are the official, state-operated law enforcement bodies tasked with upholding the legal system and maintaining public order on Earth's various cities.

Modern police forces were not founded until the 17th and 19th centuries, evolving from the first centrally organized force in Paris (1667) and the first metropolitan civil force in London (1829).

During Atom Eve’s devastating highway battle against her genetically engineered siblings, local police forces primarily played the role of helpless bystanders and active liabilities who required rescuing. Because the confrontation erupted unexpectedly amidst heavily moving highway traffic, regular law enforcement was entirely unprepared and unable to establish a prompt roadblock or safely evacuate the area. When the police attempted to intervene, they were instantly physically outmatched by the horrific, shape-shifting clones. The officers quickly shifted from responders to targets, culminating in a moment where Atom Eve had to explicitly divert her focus from the fight to deploy an energy forcefield, shielding a group of helpless police officers from a car hurled directly at them by her siblings.

In 2016, when four monsters attacked civilians on the highway, the police made a stand but were told by a girl to fall back. The commanding officer told her to leave but was convinced when she defended them from an incoming car, and the group left to form a perimeter.

Its often regarded by many of the Superheroes, civilians alike who use Reddit, that the Lizard League are treated as jokester group of jackals, not meant to be taken seriously.

One day, a punk kid deliquent, went on Reddit and discovered a "possible" but false rumor of drinking or fusing the blood of a powerful hero to become even more powerful.

entities.name: Relonian
entities.description:
The Relonians are one of the alien species to be conquered by the Viltrum Empire and were one of the species to resist their rule. In their brief appearance, they played a small but meaningful role in setting the stage with their resistance for what would ultimately lead to the Viltrumite War and the downfall of the Empire itself.

They seem to be a humanoid alien species with different skin colors, varying from green, blue, or dark yellow. They also have four horns on their heads and the sides of their jaws, with large canine teeth in their lower mouths.

Either before or after their enslavement by the Viltrumites, the Relonians wear matching dull red uniforms that cover most of their bodies, but leave their arms exposed.

It is unknown what their culture was like before they were subjugated by the Viltrumites, but they proved brave enough to resist the Viltrum Empire despite their lack of physical strength. They remained unrelenting in the face of the Viltrumites' physical superiority, continuing to fight against them despite the overwhelming odds. They also show a strong resolve in their resistance, working together against threats. While lacking physical power, the Relonians have proved themselves to be strong in their own right; they are very resourceful, concealing their plans from their oppressors and avoiding arousing suspicion until the very last moment, in which they would launch sudden attacks that would catch them off-guard.

4x02 "I'll Give You the Grand Tour" (Debut)

The Rognarrs are a savage, non-sapient alien species recognized as one of the most physically powerful species in the universe.

They are among the few beings that capable of posing a genuine threat to the Viltrum Empire, having been confronted by both Nolan and Conquest during their mission. After several of them were obtained by the Coalition of Planets they were utilized during the Viltrumite War and played a key role in the defeat of the empire.

Rognarrs are large, muscular, semi-humanoid reptilian aliens with strong pointed jaws lined with sharp teeth including distinctly enlarged incisors, possessing a dinosaurian appearance. Their bodies are primarily orange and red, patterned with darker brown markings that extend from the shoulders down their arms, legs, and tails. They possess three fingered hands with long claws, long tongues, and featureless yellow eyes.

entities.description:
Sinlak beetles are a resilient, non-sapient species known for their distinctive armored shells.

During the Viltrum Empire's campaigns, Nolan was ordered to exterminate the Sinlak beetles due to a dangerous property of their shells, though some individuals were left alive and later brought under the influence of the Coalition of Planets.

Sinlak beetles are about the size of a large dog. They have six legs and two small antennae. Their bodies are covered in green armored shells, and they have two golden eyes.

The Beetles, despite being an endangered species exhibit docile behavior and simple-minded as they are seen to be approachable to strangers, even allowing Allen to pick them up and be carried around despite their dangerous reputation. At most, they are skittish but none too bright as they are not capable of escaping danger and their best defense seems to be secreting slime.

entities.description:
The Teen Team were a group of teenage superheroes, led by Robot.

The team disbanded for a time to join the new Guardians of the Globe. After a fallout with Cecil Stedman and the Global Defense Agency, the team was restored with both old and new members joining the cause.

The Teen Team was formed at some unspecified point and comprised of four young superheroes: Atom Eve, Rex Splode, Dupli-Kate, and Robot. Mark Grayson/Invincible meets them via Atom Eve, who goes to the same high school as him.

In the absence of the Guardians of the Globe, the Teen Team fended off the oncoming Flaxan invasion. The Teen Team duel against the invading aliens, though are not well-equipped and out-numbered against them, which leads to numerous civilian casualties. However, the invading force soon begins to rapidly age due to the temporal differences between their dimension and Earth, forcing them to retreat and allow the Teen Team to succeed.

entities.name: Vile
entities.description:
The Vile are pale, hairless creatures with a large body and long, clawed limbs. They have four hands, each tipped with sharp, finger-like nails resembling claws. They also have a huge, gaping mouth filled with jagged teeth, and they have no eyes.

The Vile are ancient, primordial beings who existed during the fourth age of the world. They were immensely powerful and posed a catastrophic threat to both the surface and subterranean realms, with destructive capabilities far beyond any other known lifeform at the time. Their presence threatened the development of life and the stability of the planet itself.

To counter this threat, the demons, led by Satan, waged a long and brutal conflict against the Vile. The demons succeeded in driving them into the Under Realm, where they were imprisoned and continuously weakened through prolonged torture. Many demons sacrificed themselves to ensure the Vile remained contained, preventing them from escaping and devastating the surface world.

Though weakened and imprisoned, the Vile were not destroyed. Their survival allowed the surface world to evolve, eventually giving rise to humans, civilisation, and subsequent ages of life. During Volcanikka’s takeover of the Under Realm, one Vile attempted to emerge from the fire where it had been tortured, but Invincible intervened, punching it back down and preventing any escape.

entities.name: Viltrumite Council
entities.description:
The Viltrumite Council serves as a central governing body within the Viltrum Empire. They previously acted as advisors to Emperor Argall and now counsel the current Grand Regent, Thragg.

The Viltrumite council serves as a governing body responsible for deliberating on matters of strategy, population recovery, and enforcement of imperial policy. While it operates through collective discussion and decision-making, its authority ultimately exists under the leadership of the Grand Regent, who retains final control over major actions and directives.

The council oversees key decisions such as assigning missions, determining enforcement measures, and selecting Viltrumites for reproductive pairings with genetically compatible species as part of efforts to rebuild their population. Once decisions are reached, they are carried out under the authority of the Grand Regent and the Empire’s high-ranking officials.

Following the death of Emperor Argall, the council played a role in establishing new leadership. Thragg’s rise to Grand Regent was supported by his position within the hierarchy, as well as his demonstrated strength, combat ability, and strategic capability, which made him the most suitable candidate to lead the Empire.

entities.description:
The Viltrumite Imperial Royal Guard serves as the central protective unit of the Viltrum Empire. They were originally tasked with safeguarding Emperor Argall, and now serve under Thragg in his role as Grand Regent.

The Imperial Royal Guard is an elite defensive unit composed of highly skilled Viltrumite warriors selected for their strength, loyalty, and discipline. Their primary function is the direct protection of the empire’s supreme ruler, operating under his immediate authority.

While visually distinct, often wearing red ceremonial uniforms with hooded designs and modified insignia, their role is largely protective and ceremonial rather than administrative or strategic. They do not typically participate in governance or broader military command unless required to defend the ruler directly.

The formation of the royal guards remains unknown; however they were assisted to safekeeping their leaders like Emperor Argall.

The Invincible War was the third overarching worldwide event in Invincible, featuring all of Earth's superpowered individuals and military forces against evil variants of Invincible from across the multiverse, led by a still very much alive Angstrom Levy. The war lasted for the course of three days, with the purpose of ruining and undermining the heroic legacy of the mainstream Invincible.

Angstrom Levy targeted Invincible and his family, aiming to get revenge for what occurred after his previous plan. He was unsuccessful and suffered critical injuries, abandoned in a desolate reality.

Though the Guardians from an alternate timeline rescued Invincible, Angstrom's body remained in the remnants of the wasteland in critical condition. Barely alive, Angstrom opened a portal to a universe occupied by mysterious beings known as the Technicians. With their help, he was repaired and initiated a fresh plan to seek vengeance on Invincible.

entities.name: Attack on Talescria
entities.description:
The Attack on Talescria, also known as the Battle of Talescria, was a significant space event in Invincible and a major battle of the Viltrumite War. The conflict began with a surprise Viltrumite assault on Talescria, the homeworld and capital of the Coalition of Planets. While the attack inflicted massive destruction and heavy casualties, the Coalition ultimately repelled the invaders, forcing Grand Regent Thragg and the surviving Viltrumites to retreat to Viltrum. This event directly led to Viltrum's Cataclysm, the climactic battle on Viltrum between a few remaining Viltrumites led by Grand Regent Thragg and a Coalition of Planets strike team led by Thaedus.

After two months of intense fighting and bloodshed, the Viltrum Empire had lost control of several enslaved worlds to the Coalition of Planets, driving imperial territory to the galactic margins. The situation infuriated Grand Regent Thragg, who was perplexed by the Coalition's sudden success. General Kregg briefed the Grand Regent, explaining that the enemy's deployment of specialized tactics and powerhouses to exploit Viltrumite weaknesses was the primary source of their advantage. Despite the setback, Thragg ordered immediate preparations for a full-scale invasion of Talescria to shatter the Coalition's illusion of victory, brushing aside Kregg’s warnings about the homeworld's dense planetary defenses.

Meanwhile on Talescria, members of the Coalition Council voiced their exhaustion and despair over mounting casualties and the seemingly endless war. Thaedus, nevertheless, attempted to reassure them that victory remained within reach. At that moment, however, the second Data Twin sabotaged Talescria’s planetary defenses, allowing a lone Viltrumite Cruiser to slip into the atmosphere unopposed.

Looming over the city and casting a massive shadow across the capital, the warship opened fire and devastated the Coalition Headquarters. Although many were killed, Thaedus, Tech Jacket, General Telia, and Allen survived. Subsequently, the assault quickly escalated as multiple Viltrumites, including General Kregg, Anissa, and Lucan, deployed from the vessel while its energy weapons began bombarding Talescria Central City. Present on the command deck of the vessel, Thragg observed the attack through a tactical feed and ordered his forces to leave no one alive. Soon afterward, carrier bays opened and waves of Viltrumite slaves were deployed to support the attack, engaging Coalition troops and firing on civilians throughout the city.

The Coalition Scan Pad is a small, handheld cylinder with a white body and grey end caps. A panel near the top has four square buttons and the main chamber glows when activated.

entities.name: Conquest's Aftermath
entities.description:
Conquest's Aftermath was a minor but crucial event in Invincible, which took place after Conquest's death, during which Nolan and Oliver remained stranded on a desolate planet to ensure Mark's survival.

In the aftermath of the gruesome battle with Conquest, the focus shifts to a desolate, rocky planet. A brutally wounded Mark Grayson lies in a deep coma, barely clinging to life. Nolan carves a massive stone memorial for Conquest as a form of respect, given how Conquest was a soldier who served his empire and fought till the very end for its glory, and as a result, deserves a warrior's respect; hence, he is buried surrounded by rock pillars in the shape of their empire's symbol. Oliver strongly objects, expressing his hatred for the destruction and death Conquest caused on Earth. He points out that people hate Conquest almost as much as they hate Nolan, making it hard to understand why his father would honor him at all. Unable to leave the planet due to heavily patrolled Viltrumite airspace, Nolan and Oliver are forced to hide and wait out Mark's recovery. Oliver is deeply distraught over his brother's condition and grows impatient, frustrated that they are stuck hiding for months while the Coalition risks their lives in the escalating war.

Nolan battles a massive centipede-like creature that ultimately swallows him whole, only for him to violently burst out of its body. Oliver uses the creature’s fluids to feed Mark, though he refuses to eat himself until Nolan forces the issue.

The next day, Nolan begins training Oliver, pushing him to fight harder. Oliver lashes out emotionally, confronting Nolan about overhearing him say his Thraxan mother was a mistake. Hurt and confused, he asks if he was a mistake too, leading the young boy to believe his father is incapable of truly caring for anyone. Nolan admits his failures as a father and tries to explain himself, but Oliver isn’t ready to forgive him and flies off.

entities.name: Coordinated Efforts
entities.description:
Coordinated Efforts was a significant space event in Invincible, which resulted in the Coalition of Planets launching their ultimate strike on the Viltrum Empire's strongholds, starting with their planets. This was one of the two events that signified the twilight of the Viltrumite War, the climactic event between the Coalition of Planets and the Viltrum Empire.

Following the attack that separated the Grayson family from the Coalition and left Allen and Tech Jacket hiding underneath a Viltrumite Cruiser, the Coalition of Planets and the Viltrum Empire began preparing their forces for the coming war. As each side rallied its armies, their leaders delivered passionate speeches outlining their goals and strengthening the resolve of their followers.

On the planet Talescria, fleets of warships departed alongside Coalition soldiers armed with advanced weapons built on intelligence gathered by scientists and field agents. As the cheering crowds looked on with hope and determination, Thaedus acknowledged that the war would bring heavy casualties. Nevertheless, he declared those sacrifices a small price to pay for the ultimate defeat and humiliation of the Viltrumite Empire.

Meanwhile, Thragg addressed his own forces with absolute confidence. Surrounded by massive warships, the empire's mightiest warriors, and enslaved armies, he proclaimed that failure was not an option. He vowed that the Viltrumites would finally finish what they started, admitting that the devastation of the Scourge Virus had only fueled their hatred for the Betrayer and the Coalition. He ended his speech by roaring Argall's enduring words: "ALL IS OURS!"

entities.name: Infinity Ray Expedition
entities.description:
The Infinity Ray Expedition was a profound space event in Invincible, in which, following Nolan's enlistment into the Coalition of Planets, both he and Allen were tasked with retrieving the Infinity Ray of the fabled Space Racer, after learning of its existence, given how it could be an invaluable asset in the final battle against the Viltrum Empire. This was one of three events that signified the dawn of the Viltrumite War, the climactic event between the Coalition and the Viltrum Empire.

After departing from the Viltrumite Prison and entering the Viltrumite Cruiser, Nolan gives Allen a crash course on how the Viltrumites were nearly extinct. Even an emotional, teary Allen stated that the story had touched him in a way that made him glad to have never met his father. Thaedus commissioned General Telia, Allen, and Nolan to discreetly retrieve new weapons. With the help of Captain Pikell, they decided to locate the Infinity Ray. Their task would take a day of traveling, and Allen and Telia wasted no time with each other as if there were no tomorrow.

The following day, the Venture was able to travel to the location, albeit asteroids, with a happy Pikell assuring they had reached it, but the rest were far from satisfied.

Nolan and Allen decided to take into space and find the Infinity Ray themselves. Discovering a giant asteroid like a cave, Nolan mentions that he "previously" defeated Space Racer and buried the Racer within the asteroid, in hopes the nomad would die of starvation. They found his Infinity Ray, attempting to obtain it, only for the weapon to quickly move on its own.

entities.name: Rognarr Season
entities.description:
The Rognarr Season was a profound space event in Invincible, in which, following Space Racer's recruitment into the Coalition of Planets, Nolan, Allen, and Captain Pikell were tasked with hoarding a great number of Rognarrs from their home planet, Savage Planet, given how they could be invaluable assets in the final battle against the Viltrum Empire. This was one of three events that signified the dawn of the Viltrumite War, the climactic event between the Coalition and the Viltrum Empire.

The cosmic scavenger hunt begins following a historical deep dive into the Viltrumite population's near decimation caused by the Scourge Virus, Nolan, Allen, General Telia, and Captain Pikell partner with the Coalition of Planets to secure countermeasures against the Viltrum Empire. Drawing from secret strategic vulnerabilities listed in Nolan’s own books, they pivot from successfully recruiting Space Racer to hunting down Rognarrs on their unforgiving, frozen home planet. Because Rognarrs possess terrifying, muscular bipedal builds, lethal jaws, and claws physically sharp enough to pierce and shred a pure-blooded Viltrumite, the Coalition wants to harvest a vanguard of these beasts to serve as frontline assault hounds in the imminent Viltrumite War.

The mission relies entirely on precision: the crew must safely extract the apex predators while they remain completely frozen and dormant in the planet's vast sheets of ice. General Telia and Captain Pikell manage the atmospheric logistics from their starship, intending to minutely adjust a giant orbiting Solar Disc to warm up a localized patch of land just enough to slide a few unconscious Rognarrs directly into the cargo hold. However, communication breaks down and a reckless mistake escalates into disaster. Instead of slightly shifting the Solar Disc's position, a proton missile strike accidentally destroys the orbital reflector entirely. The resulting atmospheric shockwave triggers a rapid, uncontained global thaw that instantly snaps the massive swarm of hibernating Rognarrs awake. Even with their movement initially stiff and half-frozen, the ferocious red beasts rapidly overpower the strike team, effortlessly shrugging off Allen's brute strength and heavily injuring both space heroes.

Nolan immediately recognizes the extreme tactical danger, shouting to Allen that even two heavy hitters of their caliber stand absolutely no chance against an awakened swarm of Rognarrs. Dropping their retrieval gear, the bleeding duo abandons the extraction site to stage a desperate retreat across the snowy trenches. General Telia executes a daring, low-altitude flyby, using the Venture's heavy defensive thrusters and weapons to scare back the charging pack long enough to pull Nolan and Allen aboard the Venture. Though they escape with their lives, the high-stakes heist ends in total tactical failure as they blow atmosphere empty-handed, leaving the deadly fauna behind. This setback forces Nolan and Allen to abandon the asset completely and chart a course for Earth, realizing their ultimate hope for survival depends on recruiting Mark Grayson and Tech Jacket for the battles ahead.

entities.name: Venture
entities.description:
The Venture is a highly advanced interstellar vessel used by the Coalition of Planets during their journeys to traverse the far reaches of space.

The Venture is a sleek, gray spaceship with a rounded body, lined with glowing blue lights and equipped with three large blue thrusters. It also has a smaller ship that can detach from the main vessel.

entities.name: Viltrum's Cataclysm
entities.description:
Viltrum's Cataclysm was a significant space event in Invincible, which resulted in the climactic battle between a few Viltrumites led by Grand Regent Thragg and a Coalition of Planets' strike team led by Thaedus on Viltrum. This marked the nightfall of the Viltrumite War, along with the genesis of the Great Resurgence, the intergalactic immigration event of the surviving Viltrumites to Earth.

When the Viltrumite War broke out, the Coalition of Planets gradually gained ground against the Viltrum Empire by making use of individuals and weapons capable of actually harming Viltrumites. These assets gave them a real advantage in battle, and allowed them to progressively whittle down the Empire’s overstretched armies, despite sustaining heavy losses.

In time, the Coalition was successful in liberating a significant amount of the galaxy from Viltrumite control; Various planets were freed and their civilizations defected from the Empire and pledged their armies and resources to the Coalition war effort. At the same time, several Viltrumites were also killed in the ensuing conflicts, further diminishing the species’ already critically low numbers.

In an attempt to destroy the Coalition of Planets in a single decisive blow, Grand Regent Thragg launched a surprise attack on Talescria, the Coalition’s main headquarters and capital. The attack was made possible through a mole within the Coalition’s ranks, Data Twin II, who purposely disabled Talescria’s planetary defenses to allow a Viltrumite warship carrying Thragg and a strike force of Viltrumites to enter the Talescria’s atmosphere undetected.

entities.name: G.D.A. Moonbase
entities.description:
The G.D.A. Moonbase is the Global Defense Agency's lunar base and the new headquarters for the Guardians of the Globe.

The Moonbase is a highly advanced monitoring and operational base constructed by the Global Defense Agency (G.D.A.). It is a permanent structure built on the surface of Earth's moon, often appearing as a collection of modular, metallic buildings and scientific equipment designed to operate in a harsh environment. It lacks a grand or overly sleek design, emphasizing its nature as a functional military/scientific outpost.

The base serves as a crucial off-world installation for the G.D.A., primarily for global and orbital surveillance, strategic monitoring of potential extraterrestrial and interdimensional threats, and coordinating superhero activities from a non-Earth location.

It is equipped with cutting-edge G.D.A. technology, including advanced surveillance systems and teleportation pads, allowing for instantaneous deployment of agents and superheroes to Earth or other locations in space.

entities.name: G.D.A. Tournament Facility
entities.description:
The G.D.A. Tournament Facility was a complex that all of Earth's heroes participated in a tournament to see who would be the chosen Guardians of the Globe.

The Tryout Center is a grey and white complex, it resembled a training facility, similar to a sports arena like Football or Basketball.

Developed to train and pit heroes in a tournament.

Tournament Facility was likely made for the original Guardians of the Globe, possibly where the Immortal, Darkwing, War Woman, Red Rush, and the rest all participated and became the Guardians of the Globe.

entities.name: Guardians Headquarters
entities.description:
The Guardians Headquarters is the base of the Guardians of the Globe, funded by the Global Defense Agency.

The Original Guardians would use this base as their staging grounds to discuss, train or plan out their next moves in case the world was in danger. While each of the guardians were busy doing their personal work lives, they would all receive calls from their wrist watches to arrive to the Guardians HQ.

As all of the guardians arrived, Immortal questioned Darkwing who arrived last of this discrete meetup. But Darkwing didn't know either, and the guardians began suspect a trap, that's when Red Rush noticed a shadowy figure aiming to hit Immortal, but Red Rush saved him just in time, but the figure then reveals himself to be, Omni-Man. War Woman shouts and is the first of the Guardians to attack Omni-Man. Omni-Man takes a few hits from Darkwing, Aquarus, and Red Rush before catching him by his wrist and horrifically crushing his skull while the other Guardians watch in shock and terror.

In a combined attack, Martian Man restrains Nolan, while War Woman and Immortal begin to attack him. Omni-Man frees himself continues to progressively overpower and further slaughter them, smashing Darkwing's head against the floor, forcing his body to release a large amount of blood, and then distracting Green Ghost who catches her colleague's corpse, long to drive his fist through Green Ghost's. He uses her body as a shield against Aquarius's attack and, after dealing with War Woman's heavy strike, kills him with her mace. An enraged Martian Man once again traps and subdues Omni-Man briefly while the two remaining Guardians, The Immortal and War Woman, batter him, drawing whole puddles of blood. Eventually, Omni-Man rips Martian Man's core to pieces, punches a hole through The Immortal's stomach, and breaks War Woman's neck. The last Guardian to live, The Immortal stares at him, still conscious, and, weakly, yet decidedly asks him what drove him to commit the rampage. Omni-Man, without responding, decapitates him and, heavily injured, collapses himself in exhaustion among the remains of his betrayed friends.

entities.name: Liberation of Conquest
entities.description:
The Liberation of Conquest was a semi-crucial event in Invincible, in which, following Conquest's defeat at Invincible's hands, he was secretly imprisoned in an underground prison in the Mojave Desert, where the Global Defense Agency planned to interrogate him on how to stop the Viltrum Empire as soon as he awakened from his coma. This was one of three events that signified the dawn of the Viltrumite War, the climactic event between the Coalition and the Viltrum Empire.

After his loss to Invincible and Atom Eve, Cecil showed Conquest's corpse to Invincible, demanding that it be burned. But in actuality, his death was staged. Aware of the considerable danger of allowing him to survive for the purpose of gaining intel on the Viltrum Empire and discovering means to eventually eliminate them, Director Cecil Stedman of the Global Defense Agency incarcerated the gravely wounded Viltrumite combatant after his loss in the Block, a top-secret facility located beneath the desert. Should he try to flee or move even an inch, the whole prison would detonate. This enables the G.D.A. scientists to examine his genetic material to determine if they can create a weapon or formula capable of killing a Viltrumite.

Two weeks later, in the midst of the final Sequid invasion, Conquest fully healed from his near fatal injuries, and upon awakening, he remarked on Invincible's stupidity in keeping him alive. Then, he easily escaped into deep space without suffering any injuries from the prison's detonation, much to Cecil's chagrin and concern. To avoid Invincible's wrath, he kept Conquest's survival and escape a secret from him, especially after he killed Rus Livingston, who was being controlled by the Sequids, to stop their final invasion of Earth.

Having escaped incarceration, Conquest returned to inform his superiors about his failed mission on Earth. Upon reaching a warship, Conquest began to carefully approach the throne of his leader, expressing a somber worry of fear. General Kregg backhanded him and ordered Conquest to kneel before the Grand Regent of the Viltrum Empire, which he quickly did, trembling and pleading to be made an example for his disgraced failure from the sole Viltrumite stronger than himself, Thragg. The latter granted Conquest a reprieve for his shortcomings, as he still found him useful, and tasked him with a new assignment relating to their conflict with the Coalition of Planets.

entities.name: Murder of the Guardians of the Globe
entities.description:
The Murder of the Guardians of the Globe is the overarching event of Invincible, where Omni-Man lured the Guardians of the Globe to a deathtrap within their base of operations, this was the first plan to further weaken humanity's defenses for his other plans.

During the Guardians' downtime, each of the Guardians received a distress call to each of their emergency devices. This led them to urgently return to Guardians HQ.

Assembled and confused, their murmurs quieted as the final hero, Darkwing, entered at last. He is questioned by Immortal as to why he assembled them, only for him to reveal that he was not the one to do so, causing the Guardians to suspect a trap. A shadow assailant aims to strike Immortal, but is noticed by Red Rush who saves the hero just in time. The assailant reveals himself as Omni-Man. War Woman shouts and is the first of the Guardians to attack Omni-Man. Darkwing, Aquarius, and Red Rush individually retaliate against the rogue superhero until Omni-Man catches and kills Red Rush.

In a combined attack, Martian Man restrains Nolan, while War Woman and Immortal begin to attack him. Omni-Man frees himself continues to progressively overpower and further slaughter them. Darkwing distracts Omni-Man from killing War Woman, and attempts to execute a dropkick attack, though this fails with Omni-Man grabbing his ankle to slam him against the floor, killing the dark superhero instantly. The Viltrumite then throws Darkwing's body at Green Ghost distracting her while she catches her colleague's corpse. Omni-Man utilizes the opening and strikes her in the head, driving his hand through her skull which also kills her in an instant. He uses her body as a shield against Aquarus's attack and, after dealing with War Woman's heavy strike, kills him with her mace. An enraged Martian Man once again traps and subdues Omni-Man briefly while the two remaining Guardians, Immortal and War Woman, pummel him, causing great damage to the Viltrumite. Eventually, Omni-Man rips Martian Man's core to pieces, punches a hole through The Immortal's stomach, and breaks War Woman's neck.
